reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM - Candidate Availability; ASA Staffing Standards

description: Free-text recruiter notes regarding the candidate's availability, special circumstances, or placement preferences not captured in structured fields (e.g., 'Candidate available after current project ends mid-month; prefers no weekends').

description: Secure URL or storage path to the RTR consent document (e.g., signed PDF, DocuSign completed envelope). Confidential as it may contain candidate signature and personal details. Null when no document was captured.
reference: DocuSign CLM; SOC 2 Type II; GDPR Article 5

description: Audit timestamp recording when this RTR record was first created in the system. Distinct from grant_timestamp, which captures the real-world consent event.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; GDPR Article 5(2); CCPA

description: Indicates whether this RTR grant is subject to an active dispute, such as a competing vendor claiming prior right to represent the same candidate to the same client. True = disputed; False = undisputed.
reference: ASA Code of Ethics; VMS Program Management; Beeline VMS

description: Free-text notes documenting the outcome and resolution of an RTR dispute, including the basis for the decision (e.g., timestamp comparison, client confirmation). Populated only when dispute_flag is True.
reference: ASA Code of Ethics; VMS Program Management

business_glossary_term: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) Disposition Code
description: Standardized EEOC disposition code associated with the candidate's submittal outcome linked to this RTR, used for adverse action tracking and OFCCP/EEOC reporting. Populated after submittal disposition is determined. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: interviewed|not_selected|hired|withdrawn|no_show|position_cancelled — promote to reference product]
reference: EEOC Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures; OFCCP Compliance

description: Message ID or thread reference from the email system capturing the candidate's email-based RTR consent. Applicable when grant_method is 'email'. Used for audit evidence retrieval.
reference: OFCCP Audit Readiness; ASA Best Practices

description: The date on which the exclusivity period of the RTR grant ends, after which the candidate may be submitted by other vendors. Null when exclusivity_flag is False or exclusivity is open-ended.
reference: ASA Best Practices; VMS Program Management

description: Indicates whether the RTR grant is exclusive to this staffing firm for the specified scope, preventing the candidate from being submitted by competing vendors to the same client or requisition. True = exclusive; False = non-exclusive.
reference: ASA Best Practices; VMS Rate Management; Beeline VMS

description: The date on which the RTR grant expires and is no longer valid for new submittals. Null indicates no expiration (open-ended grant). Enforced by ATS workflow to prevent unauthorized submittals after expiry.
reference: ASA Best Practices; Co-Employment Risk Management

description: The channel or mechanism by which the candidate provided RTR consent. 'verbal' — spoken consent captured by recruiter; 'email' — written consent via email; 'portal_consent' — self-service ATS/candidate portal click-through; 'signed_form' — wet or e-signature on RTR document; 'vms_portal' — consent captured through a Vendor Management System (VMS) portal such as Beeline.
reference: ASA Code of Ethics; OFCCP Audit Readiness; DocuSign CLM

description: The exact date and time the candidate granted the Right to Represent authorization. This is the principal business event timestamp for this transaction, distinct from the record audit timestamp.
reference: ASA Best Practices; OFCCP Audit Readiness; FCRA

description: Indicates whether the candidate has revoked the RTR grant prior to its natural expiration. True = revoked; False = not revoked. Used as a fast-path filter in submittal eligibility checks.
reference: ASA Code of Ethics; OFCCP Compliance

description: Indicates whether the client requires a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) to be in place before the candidate's profile can be shared. True = NDA required prior to submittal; False = no NDA requirement.
reference: DocuSign CLM; MSA Terms; Client Program Requirements

description: Indicates whether the required NDA has been executed by the candidate prior to or concurrent with the RTR grant. Relevant when nda_required is True. True = NDA signed; False = NDA not yet signed.
reference: DocuSign CLM; OFCCP Compliance; Client MSA

description: General free-text notes entered by the recruiter or compliance team regarding this RTR grant, including any special conditions, client-specific requirements, or contextual information not captured in structured fields.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM — Notes Object; ASA Best Practices

description: Indicates whether this RTR record has all required documentation and metadata to satisfy an Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) audit, including consent evidence, timestamps, and scope definition. True = audit-ready; False = documentation incomplete.
reference: OFCCP Compliance Requirements; EEOC Guidelines; ASA Best Practices

description: The worker classification and engagement type for which the RTR is being granted. 'w2_temp' — W-2 temporary placement; '1099_contract' — independent contractor (1099); 'contract_to_hire' — contract-to-hire (temp-to-perm); 'direct_hire' — direct placement/permanent; 'eor' — Employer of Record (EOR) arrangement.
reference: IRS Worker Classification Rules; FLSA; ASA Best Practices

description: Identifies who initiated the revocation of the RTR grant. 'candidate' — candidate self-revoked; 'recruiter' — recruiter revoked on behalf of candidate; 'system' — automated revocation triggered by business rule (e.g., placement made); 'client' — client requested removal.
reference: ASA Code of Ethics; OFCCP Compliance

description: Free-text or categorized explanation provided by the candidate or recruiter for why the RTR was revoked. Examples: candidate accepted another offer, candidate withdrew from process, candidate requested removal from client consideration.
reference: ASA Code of Ethics; GDPR Article 7(3); CCPA

description: The exact date and time the candidate revoked the RTR grant. Null when is_revoked is False. Required for audit trail and to determine the window during which submittals were authorized.
reference: ASA Code of Ethics; OFCCP Audit Readiness; GDPR Article 7(3)

description: Human-readable, externally referenceable identifier for the RTR grant, used in recruiter communications, audit trails, and submittal documentation. Format: RTR-YYYY-NNNNNN.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM — Submittal Reference; ASA Best Practices

description: Defines the breadth of the RTR authorization. 'single_req' — limited to one specific requisition/job order; 'client_wide' — covers all open requisitions at the named client; 'program_wide' — covers all requisitions within a managed service program (MSP/VMS program).
reference: ASA Best Practices; Co-Employment Risk Management; Beeline VMS

description: Current lifecycle state of the RTR grant. 'active' — valid and usable for submittal; 'expired' — past expiration date; 'revoked' — candidate withdrew consent; 'pending' — awaiting candidate confirmation; 'superseded' — replaced by a newer RTR for the same scope.
reference: ASA Code of Ethics; OFCCP Compliance; EEOC Guidelines

description: Identifies the originating system where the RTR consent was captured. 'bullhorn' — Bullhorn ATS/CRM; 'beeline_vms' — Beeline VMS portal; 'candidate_portal' — self-service candidate portal; 'email' — email-based capture; 'manual' — manually entered by recruiter.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM; Beeline VMS; SOC 2 Type II

description: The native identifier of this RTR record in the originating source system (e.g., Bullhorn submittal ID, Beeline VMS consent token). Used for cross-system reconciliation and data lineage.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM; Beeline VMS; SOC 2 Type II

description: Audit timestamp recording the most recent modification to this RTR record, including status changes, revocations, or scope updates.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; GDPR Article 5(2)

description: The number of calendar days for which the RTR grant is valid from the grant_timestamp. Used to calculate expiration_date and to standardize RTR validity policies across client programs.
reference: ASA Best Practices; VMS Program Rate Management

description: Recruiter-entered notes documenting the circumstances of a verbal RTR consent, including date, time, and summary of conversation. Required when grant_method is 'verbal' to satisfy audit requirements.
reference: ASA Code of Ethics; OFCCP Audit Readiness

description: Primary key for talent_pool
Identifier of the client organization this talent pool is dedicated to, if it is a client-specific pool. Null for general pools.
Identifier of the internal team or business unit responsible for managing this talent pool.
Self-referencing FK on talent_pool (parent_talent_pool_id)
Identifier of the internal user (recruiter, account manager, or talent pool manager) who owns and manages this talent pool.
External identifier for this talent pool in the source Applicant Tracking System (e.g., Bullhorn pool ID).
The number of candidates in this talent pool who are currently available for immediate placement (not on assignment).
Specific identifier for this talent pool in the Bullhorn ATS system, supporting integration and synchronization.
The timestamp when this talent pool record was first created in the system.
The current number of active candidates assigned to this talent pool.
Detailed business description of the talent pool, including its purpose, target candidate profiles, and intended use cases.
The date when this talent pool was deactivated or archived. Null for currently active pools.
The date when this talent pool became active and available for candidate sourcing and placement activities.
The target experience or seniority level of candidates in this talent pool (entry, junior, mid-level, senior, executive, expert).
The geographic reach or coverage area of the talent pool (local, regional, national, international, remote).
Boolean flag indicating whether this talent pool represents bench candidates (employees between assignments awaiting redeployment).
Boolean flag indicating whether this talent pool is dedicated to a specific client organization.
Boolean flag indicating whether this talent pool is specifically used for redeploying existing employees to new assignments.
The date when the most recent candidate was added to this talent pool.
The timestamp when this talent pool record was last updated or modified.
The date when the most recent candidate from this talent pool was successfully placed in a position.
The maximum number of years of professional experience for candidates in this talent pool, if applicable.
The minimum number of years of professional experience required for candidates in this talent pool.
Free-text notes or comments about the talent pool, including special instructions, sourcing strategies, or business context.
The employment classification or placement model this talent pool supports (W-2 employee, 1099 contractor, Employer of Record, permanent hire, contract, temp-to-perm).
Externally-known unique code or identifier for the talent pool used in reporting and integrations.
Human-readable name of the talent pool (e.g., 'Java Developers - Senior', 'Healthcare RNs - West Coast', 'Finance Contractors - Available').
Current lifecycle status of the talent pool indicating whether it is actively used for candidate sourcing and placement.
Classification of the talent pool based on its segmentation criteria (skill-based, industry-based, geography-based, availability-based, client-specific, project-based).
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the primary geographic location of the talent pool (e.g., USA, GBR, CAN).
The primary state, province, or region within the country where this talent pool is focused.
The primary skill or competency category that defines this talent pool (e.g., 'Software Development', 'Nursing', 'Accounting').
Business priority level assigned to this talent pool for resource allocation and recruitment focus (critical, high, medium, low).
Optional secondary skill or competency category for multi-skilled talent pools.
The primary sourcing channel or method used to build this talent pool (e.g., 'Job Boards', 'Employee Referrals', 'Social Media', 'Campus Recruiting').
The target or goal number of candidates to maintain in this talent pool for optimal sourcing capacity.
The industry or sector this talent pool is designed to serve (e.g., 'Healthcare', 'Financial Services', 'Technology').
Unique surrogate identifier for each talent pool membership record. Primary key for the talent_pool_membership entity in the candidate domain Silver layer.
reference: ISO 30405:2016 Human Resource Management

description: Reference to the client account for which this talent pool is specifically curated, if applicable. Null for general or non-client-specific talent pools. Supports client-specific bench management and VMS program alignment.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM - Client Account Object; Beeline VMS

description: Foreign key linking to client.location. Business justification: Talent pools often organized by client location ("pool for Chicago warehouse site") to support targeted sourcing, redeployment, and bench management. Standard MSP/VMS practice. No existing location FK
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the recruiter or staffing coordinator who added the candidate to the talent pool. Supports accountability tracking and recruiter performance analytics.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM - User Object; ISO 30405:2016

description: Reference to the candidate who is a member of the talent pool. Links to the candidate master record in the Bullhorn ATS/CRM candidate object.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM - Candidate Object

description: Reference to the assignment that is ending and triggering the redeployment of this candidate into the talent pool. Null for non-redeployment pool memberships. Links to the placement.assignment product.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM - Placement/Assignment Object; ASA Redeployment Best Practices

description: Reference to the curated talent pool or talent community to which the candidate belongs. Talent pools may represent skill-based communities, redeployment pools, client-specific bench lists, or specialty practice groups.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM - Tearsheet/Talent Pool Object; ISO 30405:2016

description: Reference to the Vendor Management System (VMS) program associated with this talent pool membership, if the pool is managed under a Managed Service Provider (MSP) or VMS-driven contingent workforce program via Beeline VMS.
reference: Beeline VMS - Program Management; ASA MSP/VMS Program Guidelines

description: Calendar date on which the candidate was added to the talent pool. Used for tenure-in-pool analytics and redeployment SLA tracking.
reference: ISO 30405:2016; ASA Staffing Industry Best Practices

description: Date from which the candidate is available to begin a new assignment or placement. For redeployment candidates, this is typically the day after the current assignment ends. Critical for matching and dispatch workflows.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM - Candidate Availability; ISO 30405:2016

description: The type of work engagement the candidate is available for within this talent pool context. Indicates whether the candidate is seeking full-time, part-time, contract, per diem, or flexible arrangements. Supports job order matching logic.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); ASA Workforce Guidelines

description: Current status of the candidate's background check (BGC) as it pertains to eligibility for placements from this talent pool. 'clear' indicates a passed background check; 'adverse_action' indicates a disqualifying result; 'expired' indicates the BGC has exceeded its validity period. Sourced from Sterling Background Check integration.
reference: Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA); EEOC Background Check Guidelines; Sterling Background Check

description: Total number of recruiter contact attempts made to the candidate since being added to this talent pool. Used to identify unresponsive candidates and trigger escalation or exit workflows.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Activity Tracking; ASA Workforce Guidelines

description: Timestamp when this talent pool membership record was first created in the system. Represents the audit creation time in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for data lineage, audit trails, and SLA measurement.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); CCPA

description: Current status of the candidate's drug screening result as it pertains to eligibility for placements from this talent pool. 'negative' indicates a passed drug screen; 'positive' indicates a failed result; 'expired' indicates the screen has exceeded its validity period. Sourced from Sterling Background Check.
reference: DOL Drug-Free Workplace Guidelines; OSHA; Sterling Background Check; ASA Compliance Standards

description: Numeric score (0–100) reflecting the candidate's level of engagement with the talent pool, based on recruiter interactions, response rates, and activity signals. Higher scores indicate more responsive and engaged candidates. Used to prioritize outreach and predict placement likelihood.
reference: ASA Workforce Analytics; SIA KPI Framework; Bullhorn ATS/CRM Engagement Tracking

description: Current E-Verify employment authorization status for the candidate. E-Verify is the federal electronic employment eligibility verification system. Required for federal contractor placements and certain state-mandated programs. Sourced from compliance.everify_case.
reference: Immigration and Nationality Act (INA); USCIS E-Verify Program; OFCCP Compliance

description: Calendar date on which the candidate exited or was removed from the talent pool. Null if the membership is still active. Used for pool churn analysis and redeployment outcome tracking.
reference: ISO 30405:2016; ASA Workforce Guidelines

description: Reason the candidate exited the talent pool. 'placed' indicates a successful placement was made; 'declined_offer' indicates the candidate declined a placement offer; 'unresponsive' indicates the candidate became unreachable; 'disqualified' indicates the candidate no longer meets pool criteria; 'converted_to_perm' indicates a temp-to-perm conversion occurred. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: placed|declined_offer|unresponsive|disqualified|converted_to_perm|pool_dissolved|candidate_request|credential_lapse — promote to reference product]
reference: ASA Workforce Guidelines; Bullhorn ATS/CRM Disposition Codes

description: Indicates whether the candidate has a valid, completed I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification on file, confirming work authorization in the United States. Required for all W-2 placements. Sourced from compliance.i9_verification.
reference: Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) - I-9 Compliance; USCIS Form I-9; EEOC

description: Number of client interviews the candidate has completed as a result of submittals from this talent pool membership. Used to measure pool conversion effectiveness and recruiter performance.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM - Interview Tracking; SIA KPI Framework; ISO 30405:2016

description: Indicates whether this pool membership record was created as part of a formal redeployment workflow triggered by an ending assignment. True when the candidate is being actively redeployed; False for general talent pool members. Supports bench and redeployment tracking KPIs.
reference: ASA Workforce Guidelines; Bullhorn ATS/CRM Redeployment Workflow

description: Indicates whether the candidate is willing to relocate for a placement sourced from this talent pool. True if the candidate has expressed willingness to relocate; False if the candidate requires local placements only. Expands the geographic matching radius for job order fulfillment.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM - Candidate Preferences; ASA Workforce Guidelines

description: Indicates whether the candidate is willing to travel for assignments sourced from this talent pool. Relevant for travel nursing, per diem, and project-based staffing programs where travel is required.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM - Candidate Preferences; ASA Per Diem Guidelines

description: Date of the most recent recruiter contact or outreach activity with the candidate regarding this pool membership. Used to identify stale pool members who have not been contacted recently and to enforce pool maintenance SLAs.
reference: ASA Workforce Guidelines; Bullhorn ATS/CRM Activity Tracking

description: Current lifecycle status of the candidate's membership in the talent pool. 'active' indicates the candidate is actively managed within the pool; 'pending_review' indicates awaiting recruiter qualification; 'suspended' indicates temporarily paused; 'exited' indicates the candidate has been removed from the pool.
reference: ISO 30405:2016 Human Resource Management; ASA Workforce Guidelines

description: Classification of the nature of the candidate's pool membership. 'redeployment' indicates the candidate is being actively redeployed from an ending assignment; 'bench' indicates an unassigned worker available for dispatch; 'talent_community' indicates a passive talent community member; 'client_specific' indicates a pool curated for a specific client program; 'specialty_practice' indicates a domain-specific skill pool. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: redeployment|bench|talent_community|client_specific|specialty_practice|pipeline|vms_preferred|msp_approved — promote to reference product]
reference: ASA Workforce Guidelines; Bullhorn ATS/CRM Tearsheet Classification

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the pay rate values (pay_rate_min, pay_rate_max). Defaults to 'USD' for domestic U.S. operations. Supports multi-currency operations for international staffing programs.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IRS Tax Reporting Requirements

description: The maximum hourly or unit pay rate the candidate is targeting for placements sourced from this talent pool. Expressed in USD. Used alongside pay_rate_min to define the candidate's acceptable pay range for matching and negotiation.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); DOL Wage and Hour Division; ASA Pay Rate Guidelines

description: The minimum hourly or unit pay rate the candidate is willing to accept for placements sourced from this talent pool. Expressed in USD. Used by recruiters during job order matching to filter viable candidates. Supports spread and gross margin analysis.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); DOL Wage and Hour Division; ASA Pay Rate Guidelines

description: Date on which the candidate was formally qualified and approved for inclusion in this talent pool by a recruiter or pool manager. May differ from added_date if a review/approval workflow is required before activation.
reference: ISO 30405:2016; ASA Credentialing and Qualification Standards

description: The candidate's preferred city for work assignments sourced from this talent pool. Used for geographic matching of job orders to pool members. Supports workforce scheduling and dispatch workflows.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM - Candidate Preferences; ASA Workforce Guidelines

description: Two-letter U.S. state code for the candidate's preferred work location. Used for geographic filtering during job order matching and for state-specific compliance checks (SUTA, workers comp, wage-hour laws).
reference: DOL State Wage and Hour Laws; SUTA Compliance; Bullhorn ATS/CRM

description: The candidate's preferred employment classification or engagement type within this pool. Reflects whether the candidate prefers W-2 temporary, 1099 independent contractor, Employer of Record (EOR), or direct hire arrangements. Informs compliance and worker classification checks.
reference: IRS Worker Classification Rules; FLSA; ASA Workforce Guidelines

description: The primary skill category or discipline that qualifies the candidate for this talent pool (e.g., 'Information Technology', 'Healthcare - Nursing', 'Light Industrial', 'Finance & Accounting'). Used for pool segmentation and job order matching. Free-text aligned to the pool's defined skill taxonomy.
reference: ISO 30405:2016; O*NET Occupational Classification; ASA Staffing Industry Analysts

description: Recruiter-assigned priority tier indicating the urgency and desirability of placing this candidate from the pool. Tier 1 represents highest priority (e.g., actively redeploying workers with imminent assignment end dates); Tier 4 represents passive pipeline members. Drives recruiter workflow prioritization.
reference: ASA Workforce Guidelines; Staffing Industry Analysts (SIA) Talent Pool Management

description: Free-text notes entered by the recruiter or pool manager documenting the rationale for the candidate's inclusion in the talent pool, any qualification criteria met, or special considerations for placement matching.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM - Notes Object; ISO 30405:2016

description: Target date by which the recruiter aims to redeploy the candidate into a new assignment. Typically aligned with or shortly after the ending assignment's end date. Used for redeployment SLA and Time to Start (TTS) tracking.
reference: ASA Workforce Guidelines; SIA KPI Framework - Time to Start (TTS)

description: The sourcing channel or mechanism through which the candidate was identified and added to this talent pool. 'redeployment' indicates the candidate was added as part of an assignment-end redeployment workflow; 'vms_import' indicates the candidate was sourced via Beeline VMS. Supports sourcing channel attribution analytics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ats_sourcing|redeployment|referral|vms_import|job_board|direct_apply|recruiter_outreach|social_media|campus|alumni — promote to reference product]
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Source Tracking; ASA Staffing Industry Analysts (SIA) Sourcing Metrics

description: The operational system of record from which this talent pool membership record originated. Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation in the Silver layer. 'bullhorn' indicates the record was sourced from Bullhorn ATS/CRM; 'beeline_vms' indicates a VMS-managed pool imported from Beeline.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; Databricks Lakehouse Data Lineage Standards

description: The native identifier of this talent pool membership record in the originating source system (e.g., Bullhorn Tearsheet Member ID or Beeline Pool Member ID). Used for cross-system reconciliation and deduplication in the Silver layer.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; Databricks Lakehouse Data Lineage Standards

description: Number of times the candidate has been submitted (submitted to a client for consideration) from this talent pool membership. A submittal is a formal presentation of a candidate's profile to a client for a specific job order. Tracks pool productivity and Quality of Submission (QoS) metrics.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM - Submission Tracking; ASA QoS Metrics; SIA KPI Framework

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this talent pool membership record. Used for change data capture (CDC), incremental ETL processing, and audit trail maintenance in the Databricks Silver layer.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); CCPA

description: The IRS and DOL worker classification applicable to this candidate within the context of this talent pool. Determines tax treatment, benefits eligibility, and co-employment risk. 'w2_employee' indicates a W-2 temporary employee; '1099_ic' indicates an Independent Contractor (IC); 'eor' indicates Employer of Record arrangement; 'corp_to_corp' indicates a business-to-business engagement.
reference: IRS Worker Classification Rules (Section 530); FLSA; DOL; ASA Co-Employment Guidelines

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the diversity profile record. Primary key for this data product in the candidate domain Silver layer.
reference: ISO 30405:2016 Human Resource Management

description: Reference to a data subject access, deletion, or correction request that triggered a change to this diversity profile record. Links to the compliance domain privacy_request product for GDPR/CCPA audit trail.
reference: GDPR Articles 15-17; CCPA; FCRA

description: Reference to the candidate whose voluntary self-identification diversity data this record captures. Links to the core candidate profile in the candidate domain.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM; EEOC Uniform Guidelines

description: Identifier of the Affirmative Action Plan (AAP) under which this candidate's diversity data is tracked for OFCCP compliance. Links the candidate's self-ID data to the applicable AAP establishment for federal contractor reporting.
reference: OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-1; Executive Order 11246

description: Indicates whether the personally identifiable elements of this diversity profile record have been anonymized following data retention expiry or candidate deletion request. Anonymized records may be retained for aggregate statistical reporting.
reference: GDPR Article 17; CCPA; FCRA; SOC 2 Type II

description: The date on which the voluntary self-identification data was collected from the candidate. Used for compliance audit trails and to determine data currency for EEOC/OFCCP reporting cycles.
reference: EEOC EEO-1; OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-1; FCRA

description: The method by which the voluntary self-identification data was collected from the candidate. Supports audit trail and data quality assessment for EEOC/OFCCP compliance reporting.
reference: EEOC Uniform Guidelines; OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-1; FCRA

description: The operational system of record from which the self-identification data was collected or ingested. Supports data lineage and system-of-record traceability for compliance audits.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; GDPR Article 30; CCPA

description: The date on which the candidate provided consent for their diversity data to be used in reporting. Supports GDPR, CCPA, and FCRA consent audit requirements.
reference: GDPR Article 7; CCPA; FCRA; EEOC

description: Indicates whether the candidate has provided explicit consent for their voluntary self-identification data to be used in EEOC, OFCCP, and internal diversity reporting. Required for lawful use of sensitive demographic data.
reference: EEOC; OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-1; GDPR Article 7; CCPA; FCRA

description: The date on which the candidate withdrew consent for use of their diversity data in reporting. Nullable when consent has not been withdrawn. Triggers data suppression from active reporting.
reference: GDPR Article 7; CCPA; FCRA

description: The timestamp when this diversity profile record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance record-keeping requirements.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; GDPR Article 30; OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-1.12

description: The data sensitivity classification level assigned to this diversity profile record. Diversity data is classified as 'restricted' by default per EEOC, OFCCP, FCRA, and internal data governance policy to enforce access control.
reference: FCRA; EEOC; OFCCP; GDPR Article 9; CCPA; SOC 2 Type II

description: The date after which this diversity profile record must be purged or anonymized per applicable data retention policies under GDPR, CCPA, FCRA, and OFCCP record-keeping requirements. Supports automated data lifecycle management.
reference: GDPR Article 5(1)(e); CCPA; FCRA; OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-1.12; DOL

description: Voluntary self-identified disability status per ADA and Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act. Captures whether the candidate identifies as having a disability as defined under Section 503 and ADA.
reference: ADA Americans with Disabilities Act; Section 503 Rehabilitation Act; OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-741

description: Optional free-text description of the disability type if voluntarily provided by the candidate. Captured only when disability_status_code is 'yes_disability' and the candidate elects to provide additional detail.
reference: ADA; Section 503 Rehabilitation Act; OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-741

business_glossary_term: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) EEO-1 Snapshot Date
description: The workforce snapshot date used for EEO-1 Component 1 reporting, typically a pay period between October 1 and December 31. Identifies which reporting cycle this record contributes to.
reference: EEOC EEO-1 Component 1; 29 CFR Part 1602

business_glossary_term: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) Job Category Code
description: The EEOC EEO-1 job category code associated with the candidate's placement or role at time of data collection. Used to stratify diversity data by occupational category for EEO-1 Component 1 reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: exec_senior_officials|first_mid_officials|professionals|technicians|sales_workers|admin_support|craft_workers|operatives|laborers|service_workers — promote to reference product]
reference: EEOC EEO-1 Component 1; 29 CFR Part 1602

description: Version identifier of the voluntary self-identification form used to collect the data. Tracks form revisions to ensure compliance with current EEOC/OFCCP category definitions and regulatory updates.
reference: EEOC EEO-1; OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-1; OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-741

description: Voluntary self-identified gender identity of the candidate. Captured per EEOC and OFCCP reporting requirements. 'self_describe' allows free-text entry captured in gender_identity_description.
reference: EEOC EEO-1; OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-1; SHRM Gender Identity Guidelines

description: Free-text self-description of gender identity provided by the candidate when gender_identity_code is 'self_describe'. Nullable for all other gender identity codes.
reference: EEOC EEO-1; SHRM Gender Identity Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Included in Affirmative Action Plan (AAP) Flag
description: Indicates whether this candidate's diversity data was included in the OFCCP Affirmative Action Plan (AAP) for the applicable reporting establishment and year.
reference: OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-1; Executive Order 11246

description: Indicates whether this candidate's diversity data was included in the annual EEOC EEO-1 Component 1 filing. Supports compliance audit and reconciliation between headcount and filed data.
reference: EEOC EEO-1 Component 1; 29 CFR Part 1602

description: The date on which the voluntary self-identification invitation was sent to the candidate. Required for OFCCP compliance to demonstrate that candidates were invited to self-identify at the appropriate stage of the hiring process.
reference: OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-741; OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-300

description: Voluntary self-identification flag indicating whether the candidate identifies as LGBTQ+. Captured for internal diversity program tracking and inclusion reporting. Not used for EEOC/OFCCP mandatory filings.
reference: SHRM Diversity and Inclusion Guidelines; ASA Diversity Best Practices

description: Reason code explaining why no response was received from the candidate for the self-identification invitation. Nullable when response_received_flag is True. Supports OFCCP audit documentation.
reference: OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-741; OFCCP 41 CFR Part 60-300

description: Free-text notes entered by compliance or HR staff regarding this diversity profile record. May include data quality observations, correction history, or compliance review comments. Access restricted per data classification policy.

description: Foreign key linking to the task checklist template that requires this credential

description: Current lifecycle status of this credential requirement. Values: active (currently enforced), inactive (not enforced, may be reactivated), pending (scheduled to become active), superseded (replaced by a newer version of the requirement).

Indicates whether failure to meet this credential requirement blocks progression or completion of the checklist (True) or is tracked as non-compliant but does not prevent checklist completion (False). When True and is_mandatory is True, the worker cannot be placed or onboarded until this credential is verified. Drives workflow gating logic.

Number of days relative to the checklist start date (typically assignment start date or onboarding initiation date) by which this credential must be verified and compliant. Negative values indicate credential must be verified before checklist start (e.g., -7 means 7 days before assignment start). Positive values allow verification after start (e.g., 30 means within 30 days of assignment start). Zero means must be verified by start date.

Date from which this credential requirement becomes active for this checklist template. Supports versioning and phased rollout of new credential requirements (e.g., new client contract effective date, new regulatory requirement effective date).

Date after which this credential requirement is no longer active for this checklist template. Nullable for ongoing requirements. Supports sunsetting of requirements when contracts end or regulations change.
Indicates whether this credential is mandatory (True) or optional/recommended (False) for completion of this specific checklist. Drives enforcement logic and blocking behavior.

Free-text field for additional context, special instructions, or exceptions related to this credential requirement for this checklist. May include client-specific instructions, alternative verification methods, or conditional logic notes.

description: Date the individualized assessment was completed. Nullable when no individualized assessment was required (e.g., non-criminal BGC findings). Documents the timeline of the EEOC-compliant review process.

reference: SAP SuccessFactors — Benefits Administration; IRS Publication 15-B; ACA Special Enrollment Rules

description: Date on which the worker's benefit enrollment ended, triggering cessation of premium withholding. Populated when a worker loses eligibility, voluntarily cancels coverage, or separates from employment. Null if enrollment is ongoing. Null for non-benefit deductions.
reference: SAP SuccessFactors — Benefits Administration; ERISA; COBRA; ACA

description: Name of the court, government agency, or child support enforcement agency that issued the garnishment order (e.g., 'Cook County Circuit Court', 'IRS', 'Illinois DCSS'). Used for remittance routing and compliance documentation. Null for non-garnishment deductions.
reference: DOL Wage Garnishment Rules; IRS Tax Levy; Child Support Enforcement (Title IV-D)

description: Date by which the withheld garnishment amount must be remitted to the issuing court or agency. Derived from the court order terms and state-specific remittance deadlines. Null for non-garnishment deductions.
reference: DOL Wage Garnishment Rules; Consumer Credit Protection Act Title III; State Garnishment Remittance Laws

description: Indicates whether this deduction line represents a recovery of a previously missed (arrears) deduction amount rather than a standard current-period deduction. True when the deduction_amount includes or consists entirely of arrears recovery. Used to distinguish regular deductions from catch-up withholdings in payroll analytics.
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Arrears Recovery; DOL Wage Garnishment Rules

business_glossary_term: Is FICA (Federal Insurance Contributions Act) Exempt Flag
description: Indicates whether this deduction amount is exempt from FICA (Social Security and Medicare) taxes. True for qualified Section 125 benefit deductions and HSA employer contributions. False for most other deductions. Drives FICA taxable wage base calculation in payroll processing.
reference: IRS FICA Rules; IRS Section 125; IRS Publication 15; FICA (26 U.S.C. § 3101)

description: Indicates whether this deduction reduces the worker's taxable gross wages before FICA, federal income tax, and applicable state income tax are calculated. True for Section 125 cafeteria plan deductions (medical, dental, vision, FSA), traditional 401k contributions, and HSA contributions. False for post-tax deductions such as Roth 401k and after-tax life insurance. Critical for accurate gross-to-net payroll calculation.
reference: IRS Section 125 (Cafeteria Plans); IRS Publication 15; IRS Publication 15-B; FICA

description: Sequential ordering number of this deduction line within the parent paycheck. Enables ordered display of deductions on pay stubs and supports reconciliation of multiple deductions per pay period. TRANSACTION_LINE role: LINE_SEQUENCE.
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Pay Stub Line Ordering

description: Last calendar date of the pay period in which this deduction line was applied. Defines the close of the earnings window for this deduction calculation. Used in conjunction with pay_period_start_date for period boundary validation and compliance reporting.
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Pay Period Definition; FLSA Record-Keeping Requirements

description: First calendar date of the pay period in which this deduction line was applied. Combined with pay_period_end_date, defines the earnings period for which this deduction is calculated. Supports multi-state payroll compliance and period-over-period deduction analysis.
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Pay Period Definition; FLSA Record-Keeping Requirements

description: Operational system of record from which this deduction line record originated. Primarily TempWorks Payroll for payroll-processed deductions, SAP SuccessFactors for benefit enrollment-driven deductions, or manual for corrections entered directly. Supports data lineage and reconciliation in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: TempWorks Payroll; SAP SuccessFactors; Databricks Lakehouse Data Lineage Standards

description: Date on which this deduction arrangement was or is scheduled to be permanently stopped. For benefit deductions, aligns with benefit enrollment termination or coverage end date. For garnishments, the date the order is satisfied or released. Null if the deduction is ongoing with no defined end.
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Deduction Termination; DOL Wage Garnishment Rules; IRS Publication 15-B

description: Timestamp when this deduction line record was last modified in the source payroll system (e.g., amount correction, status change, suspension). Supports change data capture (CDC) processing in the Databricks Silver Layer and audit trail requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: SOC 2 Type II Audit Trail Requirements; GDPR Article 5; TempWorks Payroll

business_glossary_term: W-2 (Wage and Tax Statement) Box Code
description: IRS W-2 form box code under which this deduction amount must be reported at year-end (e.g., 'D' for 401k elective deferrals, 'W' for HSA employer contributions, 'DD' for employer-sponsored health coverage cost). Drives W-2 generation in TempWorks Payroll. Null for deductions not reportable on W-2.
reference: IRS W-2 Instructions; IRS Publication 15-B; W-2 Box 12 Codes

description: Two-letter U.S. state code for the state in which the worker performed services during this pay period. Determines applicable state income tax withholding rules, state-specific garnishment limits, SUTA taxability, and state benefit deduction regulations. Critical for multi-state payroll compliance.
reference: IRS Publication 15; SUTA State Regulations; Multi-State Payroll Compliance; DOL State Wage Laws

description: Cumulative total of this deduction withheld from the worker's pay from the start of the calendar year through and including the current pay period. Used for W-2 reporting, IRS annual contribution limit enforcement (e.g., 401k IRS limit, FSA/HSA annual caps), and year-end tax reconciliation.
reference: IRS Publication 15; IRS 401(k) Contribution Limits; IRS FSA/HSA Annual Limits; W-2 Reporting Requirements

description: Unique system-generated surrogate key identifying a single court-ordered or agency-mandated wage garnishment record in the TempWorks Payroll system. TRANSACTION_HEADER primary key.
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Garnishment Module

description: Foreign key linking to placement.assignment. Business justification: Garnishment orders follow worker across assignments. Links order to current assignment for payroll withholding processing, remittance tracking, and compliance with court orders during active placement
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to placement.direct_hire. Business justification: Direct hire employees may have garnishment orders. When staffing firm processes payroll for direct hires, garnishments must be withheld and remitted. Links order to permanent placement.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Garnishments post to liability accounts (garnishment payable) for balance sheet reporting and remittance tracking. Required for accurate liability reporting and compliance with court-ordered withholdi
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the payroll company or legal entity within TempWorks Payroll responsible for processing this garnishment. Relevant for multi-entity staffing organizations where workers may be employed under different legal entities (e.g., EOR entities, co-employment entities).
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Company Setup; EOR (Employer of Record) Model

description: Foreign key linking to onboarding.onboarding_engagement. Business justification: Garnishment orders received during pre-employment screening or at hire must be linked to onboarding engagement for compliance documentation. Supports audit trail showing when garnishment was identifie
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the worker (employee or contractor) whose wages are subject to this garnishment order. Links to the worker master record in TempWorks Payroll / SAP SuccessFactors.
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Employee Master; FLSA 29 CFR Part 870

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_violation. Business justification: Garnishment orders may result from regulatory violations (child support enforcement failures, tax liens, court-ordered restitution). Compliance tracking links enforcement actions to payroll deduction
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Dollar amount of the per-pay-period administrative fee the employer is permitted to charge the employee for processing the garnishment, as allowed by applicable state law. Typically $1–$5 per pay period. Zero if the state does not permit an administrative fee.
reference: State Wage Garnishment Laws; FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; ASA Compliance Guidelines

description: Dollar amount of past-due arrears included in the garnishment order, separate from the current ongoing obligation. Particularly relevant for child support orders where arrears withholding may be calculated at a different rate than current support.
reference: Title IV-D Child Support Enforcement; FLSA 29 CFR Part 870

description: The timestamp when this garnishment order record was first created in the TempWorks Payroll system. Serves as the audit trail creation marker per SOC 2 Type II and internal data governance requirements.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; GDPR Article 5(2); CCPA

description: The date on which withholding under this garnishment order must begin, as specified by the issuing authority. Payroll must begin deducting no later than the first pay period that includes this date.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; IRS Publication 1494; Title IV-D

description: The actual date on which the employer submitted its response to the issuing authority. Used to verify timely compliance with mandatory response deadlines and to support audit documentation.
reference: Title IV-D; OMB Form 0970-0154; FLSA 29 CFR Part 870

description: The deadline by which the employer must respond to the issuing authority confirming receipt and intent to comply with the garnishment order, or to contest the order if applicable. Typically within 10–15 business days of receipt for IWOs.
reference: Title IV-D; OMB Form 0970-0154; IRS Publication 1494

description: The date on which the garnishment order expires or is scheduled to end. Null for open-ended orders (e.g., ongoing child support). Payroll must cease withholding after this date unless a renewal order is received.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; IRS Publication 1494

description: Current lifecycle status of the garnishment order. Active: withholding is in progress. Suspended: temporarily halted per court or agency instruction. Satisfied: total obligation has been fully paid. Terminated: order cancelled or revoked. Pending: received but not yet activated in payroll.
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Garnishment Module; FLSA 29 CFR Part 870

description: Classification of the garnishment by legal category. Determines applicable withholding limits and priority rules under federal and state law. Values: child_support (Title IV-D orders), creditor_garnishment (civil court judgment), student_loan (Department of Education administrative garnishment), tax_levy (IRS or state tax levy), bankruptcy (Chapter 13 trustee payment).
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; IRS Publication 1494; Title IV-D Child Support Enforcement; 20 U.S.C. § 1095a (HEA); 11 U.S.C. § 1325 (Bankruptcy)

description: Indicates whether this garnishment order includes or is exclusively for past-due arrears (True) versus a current ongoing obligation only (False). Relevant for child support orders where arrears withholding may trigger a higher CCPA cap (up to 65% vs. 50%).
reference: CCPA 15 U.S.C. § 1673; Title IV-D; FLSA 29 CFR Part 870

description: Indicates whether this garnishment is an Income Withholding Order (IWO) issued under Title IV-D of the Social Security Act (True). IWOs have specific federal processing requirements including mandatory employer response timelines and standardized form usage (OMB 0970-0154).
reference: Title IV-D; 42 U.S.C. § 666(b); OMB Form 0970-0154

description: Name of the court, government agency, or administrative body that issued the garnishment order (e.g., 'Cook County Circuit Court', 'IRS — Automated Collection System', 'Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services — Child Support Division').
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; IRS Publication 668-W; Title IV-D

description: Two-letter U.S. state or territory code of the jurisdiction that issued the garnishment order. Used to apply the correct state-specific withholding limits and priority rules, which may be more protective than federal CCPA limits.
reference: CCPA 15 U.S.C. § 1673; State Wage Garnishment Laws

description: Version identifier of the standardized federal Income Withholding Order form used (e.g., 'OMB 0970-0154 Rev. 06/2021'). Required for audit and compliance tracking of IWO processing. Null when is_income_withholding_order is False.
reference: Title IV-D; OMB Form 0970-0154; OCSE (Office of Child Support Enforcement)

description: The maximum percentage of disposable earnings that may be withheld under this order, as governed by the Consumer Credit Protection Act (CCPA) and FLSA. Stored as a decimal fraction (e.g., 0.50 = 50%). Payroll must not exceed this cap even if the ordered amount would otherwise require it. Defaults vary by garnishment type (e.g., 50–65% for child support, 25% for creditor garnishments).
reference: CCPA 15 U.S.C. § 1673; FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; DOL Fact Sheet #30

description: Free-text field for payroll staff to record additional context, special instructions from the issuing authority, or internal processing notes related to this garnishment order (e.g., 'Worker contested order — awaiting court ruling', 'SDU requires paper check until EFT enrollment complete').
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Garnishment Module

description: The externally-issued case or order number assigned by the issuing court, agency, or government authority (e.g., court docket number, IRS levy notice number, state child support case number). This is the primary business identifier used to cross-reference with the issuing authority.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; IRS Publication 1494; CCPA 15 U.S.C. § 1673

description: Integer ranking that determines the sequence in which this garnishment is applied when a worker has multiple simultaneous garnishment orders. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Child support orders are federally mandated to take priority over other garnishments. Used by payroll to allocate available disposable earnings across competing orders.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; CCPA 15 U.S.C. § 1673; Title IV-D

description: The date on which the employer (Staffing Hr) received the garnishment order from the issuing authority. Triggers the employer's legal obligation to begin withholding within the required timeframe. Distinct from the effective_date specified in the order.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; Title IV-D; IRS Publication 1494

description: Bank account number for EFT/ACH remittance to the garnishment payee. Stored in masked or tokenized form per PCI/security policy. Null when remittance_method is 'check'.
reference: Title IV-D; IRS Publication 1494; PCI DSS

description: Primary street address line for mailing garnishment remittance payments to the payee. Used when electronic remittance (EFT/EFT) is not available.
reference: Title IV-D; IRS Publication 1494

description: Secondary address line (suite, PO Box, unit number) for the garnishment remittance payee mailing address.
reference: Title IV-D; IRS Publication 1494

description: City of the garnishment remittance payee mailing address.
reference: Title IV-D; IRS Publication 1494

description: How frequently withheld garnishment funds must be remitted to the payee. Most child support SDUs require remittance within 7 business days of the pay date. IRS levies may require per-payroll remittance.
reference: Title IV-D (7-day SDU rule); IRS Publication 1494

description: Method by which withheld garnishment funds are transmitted to the remittance payee. EFT/ACH is required for most State Disbursement Units (SDUs) under Title IV-D. Check is used for payees that do not accept electronic payment.
reference: Title IV-D (SDU EFT requirement); IRS Publication 1494

description: Name of the entity to whom withheld funds must be remitted (e.g., 'State Disbursement Unit — Illinois', 'IRS — ACS', 'Chapter 13 Trustee — Northern District of Illinois'). Used to generate the payable in Oracle NetSuite ERP accounts payable.
reference: Title IV-D (SDU requirement); IRS Publication 1494; 11 U.S.C. § 1325

description: Payee-assigned reference code or FIPS code that must appear on each remittance payment to allow the receiving agency to correctly apply the payment to the correct case (e.g., SDU case number, IRS notice number, FIPS employer code).
reference: Title IV-D; IRS Publication 1494

description: ABA routing transit number for EFT/ACH remittance to the garnishment payee. Nine-digit number identifying the receiving financial institution. Null when remittance_method is 'check'.
reference: Title IV-D; IRS Publication 1494; Federal Reserve Regulation J

description: Two-letter U.S. state or territory code of the garnishment remittance payee mailing address.
reference: Title IV-D; IRS Publication 1494

description: ZIP or ZIP+4 postal code of the garnishment remittance payee mailing address.
reference: Title IV-D; IRS Publication 1494

description: The native record identifier assigned by TempWorks Payroll to this garnishment order in the operational system of record. Used for lineage tracing, reconciliation, and re-ingestion deduplication in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Garnishment Module; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Conventions

description: Free-text description of the reason the garnishment order was suspended (e.g., 'Court-ordered stay pending appeal', 'Worker on unpaid leave — no disposable earnings', 'Agency-issued suspension notice received'). Populated only when status is 'suspended'.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; TempWorks Payroll — Garnishment Module

description: The date on which the garnishment order was terminated, satisfied, or revoked, resulting in cessation of withholding. Populated when status transitions to 'satisfied' or 'terminated'. Null while the order is active or pending.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; IRS Publication 1494

description: The total dollar amount owed under this garnishment order as specified by the issuing authority (e.g., total judgment debt, total child support arrears). Null for ongoing orders with no defined total (e.g., current child support with no arrears). Used to determine when the order is satisfied.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; IRS Publication 1494

description: Cumulative dollar amount withheld from the worker's pay and remitted under this garnishment order since the effective date. Updated each payroll cycle. Used to track progress toward satisfying the total obligation and to determine when the order is fully paid.
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Garnishment Module; FLSA 29 CFR Part 870

description: The timestamp when this garnishment order record was most recently modified in the TempWorks Payroll system. Used for change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver Layer pipeline and for audit trail compliance.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; GDPR Article 5(2); TempWorks Payroll — Garnishment Module

description: Fixed dollar amount to be withheld from the worker's pay per pay period when withholding_method is 'fixed_amount'. Null when withholding_method is 'percentage'. Expressed in USD.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; IRS Publication 1494; CCPA 15 U.S.C. § 1673

description: Indicates whether the garnishment is calculated as a fixed dollar amount per pay period or as a percentage of the worker's disposable earnings. Determines which of the two withholding fields (withholding_amount or withholding_percentage) is operative.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; CCPA 15 U.S.C. § 1673

description: Percentage of the worker's disposable earnings to be withheld per pay period when withholding_method is 'percentage'. Stored as a decimal fraction (e.g., 0.25 = 25%). Null when withholding_method is 'fixed_amount'.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 870; CCPA 15 U.S.C. § 1673; Title IV-D

description: Primary key for wc_policy

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Workers comp premiums are allocated to cost centers for burden calculation and client billing. Required for accurate cost center profitability and pricing in staffing operations with varying risk prof
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Workers comp premiums post to insurance expense GL accounts for P&L reporting and cost allocation. Required for accurate expense classification and burden rate calculation in staffing operations with
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to client.location. Business justification: Workers' comp policies are jurisdiction-specific and tied to specific work locations. Required for accurate premium calculation, state compliance, and tracking which client locations are covered under
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.osha_incident. Business justification: Workers' comp policies are triggered by OSHA recordable incidents. Claim filing, reserve setting, and premium adjustments depend on incident data - operational link between safety incident tracking an
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to payroll.pay_run. Business justification: Workers compensation premium calculations are tied to specific payroll runs. wc_policy currently has pay_run_reference: STRING which is a denormalized reference. Adding structured FK pay_run_id → pay_
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to vendor.supplier. Business justification: Workers' comp policies for vendor-supplied workers are often held by the vendor, not the staffing agency. Certificate of insurance (COI) tracking, premium audit, and liability determination require li
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to placement.work_location. Business justification: Workers compensation policies are issued per work location and jurisdiction. Each site has specific WC class codes and rates. Links policy coverage to physical work location.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: The dollar amount of premium adjustment resulting from the most recent carrier audit, representing the difference between estimated premiums paid and actual earned premium based on audited payroll. Positive values indicate additional premium owed; negative values indicate a return premium credit.
reference: NCCI Basic Manual for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance; TempWorks Payroll - Workers Compensation Module

description: The frequency at which the insurance carrier conducts a premium audit to reconcile estimated premiums against actual payroll. Staffing firms with high payroll volume often negotiate more frequent audits to reduce year-end true-up exposure.
reference: NCCI Basic Manual for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance; ASA Risk Management Standards

business_glossary_term: Workers Compensation (WC) Base Rate per $100 of Payroll
description: The manual (base) WC premium rate expressed as a dollar amount per $100 of covered payroll for the associated class code and state jurisdiction, before application of the experience modification factor (EMR). Sourced from the applicable state rating bureau or NCCI.
reference: NCCI Experience Rating Plan Manual; State Workers Compensation Rating Bureaus

description: The WC premium cost expressed as a decimal rate applied to gross payroll, representing the WC component of the total employer burden rate. Used in bill rate calculations, spread analysis, and gross margin reporting. Derived from the modified rate and historical payroll mix for this class code.
reference: ASA Staffing Industry Financial Benchmarks; TempWorks Payroll - Burden Rate Configuration

business_glossary_term: Insurance Carrier National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) Code
description: The five-digit NAIC company code assigned to the insurance carrier by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners. Used for regulatory identification and carrier verification in multi-state WC compliance.
reference: NAIC Company Code Registry; State Insurance Department Regulations

description: The legal name of the insurance carrier or underwriter providing the workers compensation coverage under this policy. Used for carrier reporting, premium remittance, and audit correspondence.
reference: NAIC (National Association of Insurance Commissioners) Carrier Registry

description: The internal cost allocation code used to attribute WC premium costs to specific client accounts or job orders. Enables client-level WC cost reporting, profitability analysis, and accurate bill rate construction inclusive of WC burden.
reference: Oracle NetSuite ERP - Cost Allocation Module; ASA Staffing Industry Financial Benchmarks

description: Indicates whether this WC policy record involves a co-employment arrangement where both the staffing firm and the client share employer responsibilities. Affects WC coverage determination and premium allocation between parties.
reference: ASA Co-Employment Guidelines; DOL Joint Employment Standards; EEOC Co-Employment Guidance

description: The calculated WC premium dollar amount for the premium period, computed as (payroll_subject_to_wc / 100) multiplied by the modified_rate_per_100. Represents the accrued WC cost for the period and is used in burden rate application and client cost allocation.
reference: NCCI Basic Manual for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance; TempWorks Payroll - Workers Compensation Module

description: The timestamp when this workers compensation policy record was first created in the payroll system. Provides audit trail for record provenance and data lineage in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: SOC 2 Type II Audit Trail Requirements; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Accountability)

business_glossary_term: Workers Compensation (WC) Deductible Amount Per Claim
description: The per-claim deductible amount the employer is responsible for funding before the carrier pays WC benefits, applicable to large deductible programs. Zero for guaranteed cost policies. Impacts cash flow planning and loss reserve requirements.
reference: NCCI Large Deductible Program Guidelines; ASA Risk Management Standards

description: The initial deposit premium paid to the carrier at policy inception, typically a percentage of the estimated annual premium. Represents the upfront cash outlay and is reconciled against actual earned premium at audit.
reference: NCCI Basic Manual for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance

description: The date on which the workers compensation insurance policy becomes active and coverage begins. Used to determine coverage applicability for worker assignments and premium period calculations.
reference: NCCI Workers Compensation Insurance Guidelines; DOL Workers Compensation Compliance

description: The aggregate policy limit of employers liability coverage for bodily injury by disease. Distinct from the per-accident limit and the per-employee disease limit. Used for risk management reporting and MSA compliance verification.
reference: NCCI Basic Manual for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance

description: The per-occurrence limit of employers liability coverage (Part B of the WC policy) for bodily injury by accident. Standard limits are $100,000, $500,000, or $1,000,000. Used for risk management and client contract compliance.
reference: NCCI Basic Manual for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance; OSHA Compliance

description: Indicates whether this WC policy record applies to workers placed under an Employer of Record (EOR) arrangement, where the staffing firm acts as the legal employer for WC purposes. Drives co-employment risk management and premium allocation logic.
reference: ASA Co-Employment Guidelines; IRS Worker Classification Rules; DOL Joint Employment Standards

description: The estimated total annual WC premium for this policy as projected at policy inception, based on estimated payroll and applicable rates. Used for budgeting, cash flow planning, and comparison against actual accrued premiums during the audit cycle.
reference: NCCI Basic Manual for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance; ASA Risk Management Standards

description: The experience modification rate (EMR) assigned by NCCI or the applicable state rating bureau, reflecting the employer's actual loss history relative to expected losses for the class. A factor below 1.0 indicates better-than-average loss experience; above 1.0 indicates worse. Applied to the base rate to compute the modified premium rate.
reference: NCCI Experience Rating Plan Manual; ASA Risk Management Standards

description: The date on which the workers compensation insurance policy expires and coverage ends. Triggers renewal workflow and is used to validate coverage during assignment management and payroll processing.
reference: NCCI Workers Compensation Insurance Guidelines; DOL Workers Compensation Compliance

business_glossary_term: Last Workers Compensation (WC) Premium Audit Date
description: The date of the most recently completed premium audit conducted by the insurance carrier. Used to track audit cycle compliance, identify overdue audits, and reconcile estimated versus actual premium balances.
reference: NCCI Basic Manual for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance; ASA Risk Management Standards

description: For loss-sensitive policies, identifies the specific program structure. Retrospective rated programs adjust final premium based on actual losses; large deductible programs require the employer to fund losses up to a deductible threshold. Null or 'none' for guaranteed cost policies.
reference: NCCI Retrospective Rating Plan Manual; ASA Risk Management Standards

description: The minimum premium amount guaranteed to the carrier regardless of actual payroll volume, as stipulated in the policy terms. Relevant for low-volume periods and ensures the carrier recovers minimum administrative costs.
reference: NCCI Basic Manual for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance

business_glossary_term: Workers Compensation (WC) Modified Rate per $100 of Payroll
description: The effective WC premium rate per $100 of payroll after applying the experience modification factor (EMR) to the base rate. This is the rate used in actual premium calculations for payroll runs. Computed as base_rate_per_100 multiplied by experience_mod_factor.
reference: NCCI Experience Rating Plan Manual; TempWorks Payroll - Workers Compensation Module

business_glossary_term: National Council on Compensation Insurance (NCCI) Class Code Description
description: The standard NCCI descriptive label for the workers compensation class code, as defined in the NCCI Scopes Manual. Provides human-readable context for the class code used in carrier reporting, premium audits, and cost allocation to client assignments.
reference: NCCI Scopes Manual

business_glossary_term: Next Scheduled Workers Compensation (WC) Premium Audit Date
description: The scheduled date for the next premium audit by the insurance carrier. Used for audit preparation planning, payroll record retention compliance, and proactive reconciliation of estimated versus actual premiums.
reference: NCCI Basic Manual for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance

business_glossary_term: Payroll Amount Subject to Workers Compensation (WC)
description: The gross payroll dollar amount for the premium period that is subject to workers compensation premium calculation for this class code and state jurisdiction. Excludes non-covered remuneration per NCCI rules (e.g., tips, certain overtime premiums). Used as the basis for premium computation.
reference: NCCI Basic Manual for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance; IRS Publication 15

description: Free-text field for operational notes, underwriting conditions, endorsements, or special program terms associated with this WC policy record. Used by payroll and risk management teams to document carrier-specific requirements or exceptions.
reference: TempWorks Payroll - Workers Compensation Module

description: The externally-assigned policy number issued by the insurance carrier that uniquely identifies this workers compensation insurance policy. Used for carrier reporting, premium audit reconciliation, and regulatory filings.
reference: American Staffing Association (ASA); NCCI Workers Compensation Insurance Guidelines

description: Current lifecycle state of the workers compensation policy. Active policies are in force and covering workers; expired policies have passed their expiration date; cancelled policies were terminated before expiration; pending policies are bound but not yet effective.
reference: TempWorks Payroll - Workers Compensation Module; DOL Workers Compensation Compliance

description: Classification of the WC insurance policy structure. Guaranteed cost policies have fixed premiums; loss-sensitive policies (e.g., retrospective rated, large deductible) have premiums that vary based on actual loss experience. Drives premium calculation methodology and financial risk exposure.
reference: NCCI Workers Compensation Insurance Guidelines; ASA Risk Management Standards

description: The four-digit calendar or fiscal year of the workers compensation policy period. Used to group premium transactions for annual audit reconciliation, loss run reporting, and year-over-year cost trend analysis.
reference: NCCI Experience Rating Plan Manual; ASA Risk Management Standards

description: The basis on which WC premiums are calculated. In staffing, the standard basis is payroll (gross remuneration subject to WC), but some specialty programs may use flat or per-capita bases. Determines how payroll_subject_to_wc is computed.
reference: NCCI Basic Manual for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance

business_glossary_term: Workers Compensation (WC) Premium Period End Date
description: The end date of the payroll period for which this WC premium transaction was calculated. Together with premium_period_start_date, defines the coverage window for the premium accrual.
reference: TempWorks Payroll - Workers Compensation Module; NCCI Basic Manual

business_glossary_term: Workers Compensation (WC) Premium Period Start Date
description: The start date of the payroll period for which this WC premium transaction was calculated. Defines the coverage window for the premium accrual and aligns with the pay run cycle.
reference: TempWorks Payroll - Workers Compensation Module; NCCI Basic Manual

description: The schedule rating credit (negative value) or debit (positive value) percentage applied to the manual premium, reflecting underwriter judgment on risk characteristics not captured by the experience modification factor. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., -0.10 for a 10% credit).
reference: NCCI Basic Manual for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance; State Rating Bureau Filings

description: The two-letter US state code representing the state jurisdiction under which this workers compensation policy is filed and governed. Critical for multi-state WC compliance, SUTA alignment, and state-specific rate application for temporary and contract workers.
