description: Username or employee ID of the payroll supervisor or manager who reviewed and approved this withholding election entry. Required for IRS lock-in letter overrides and exempt status elections as part of internal controls.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; TempWorks Payroll Audit Trail; IRS Publication 15-T

description: Timestamp when this withholding election record was first created in the payroll system. Supports audit trail, SOC 2 Type II compliance, and IRS record retention requirements for withholding forms.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; IRS Publication 15-T Record Retention; TempWorks Payroll

description: Dollar amount of itemized or other deductions entered in Step 4b of the 2020+ W-4. Reduces withholding by accounting for deductions that exceed the standard deduction. Null for pre-2020 W-4 forms.
reference: IRS W-4 Step 4b (2020+); IRS Publication 15-T; IRS Schedule A

description: Dollar amount of qualifying dependent credits entered in Step 3 of the 2020+ redesigned W-4. Reduces the amount of income subject to withholding. Includes child tax credit ($2,000 per qualifying child under 17) and other dependent credits ($500 per other dependent). Null for pre-2020 W-4 forms.
reference: IRS W-4 Step 3 (2020+); IRS Publication 972; IRS Publication 15-T

description: Reference identifier for the physical or electronic withholding form document stored in the document management system (e.g., DocuSign CLM or SAP SuccessFactors document repository). Enables retrieval of the original signed form for audit and compliance verification.
reference: DocuSign CLM; SAP SuccessFactors Onboarding; IRS Record Retention Requirements; FCRA

description: Date on which this withholding election becomes effective and begins driving tax withholding calculations in pay runs. Aligns with IRS requirement that new W-4 elections take effect no later than the start of the first payroll period ending on or after the 30th day after the form is received.
reference: IRS Publication 15-T; IRS W-4 Instructions; TempWorks Payroll

description: Free-text notes entered by payroll staff regarding this withholding election. May include reasons for IRS lock-in overrides, documentation of verbal instructions, or notes on unusual withholding configurations.
reference: TempWorks Payroll - Tax Withholding Module; SOC 2 Type II

description: Externally-visible business identifier for this withholding election record, used for audit trails, payroll processing references, and worker communications (e.g., TWE-2024-00123).
reference: TempWorks Payroll - Tax Withholding Module; IRS Publication 15-T

description: The channel or method through which the withholding election was submitted. Paper form = physical W-4 or state form submitted; Electronic self-service = worker submitted via online portal (e.g., SAP SuccessFactors ESS); Employer default = system default applied when no form received; IRS lock-in = IRS-mandated withholding rate overriding worker election; Verbal instruction = documented verbal request.
reference: IRS Publication 15-T; SAP SuccessFactors Onboarding; TempWorks Payroll; FCRA

description: Current lifecycle state of this withholding election. Active = currently driving withholding calculations; Superseded = replaced by a newer election; Pending = submitted but not yet effective; Cancelled = voided before taking effect; Expired = past the expiration date.
reference: TempWorks Payroll - Tax Withholding Module; IRS Publication 15-T

description: Sequential version number for withholding elections for the same worker and jurisdiction. Increments each time the worker submits a new withholding form. Enables tracking of election history and supersession chain for audit and compliance purposes.
reference: TempWorks Payroll - Tax Withholding Module; IRS Publication 15-T Record Retention

description: Username or employee ID of the payroll staff member or system process that entered this withholding election into TempWorks Payroll. Supports audit trail requirements for payroll compliance and SOC 2 Type II controls.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; TempWorks Payroll Audit Trail; IRS Publication 15-T Record Retention

description: Date on which this withholding election expires and is no longer valid. Applicable for exempt-from-withholding elections which expire annually (February 15 of the following year per IRS rules), or for state-specific elections with defined validity periods.
reference: IRS Publication 15-T; IRS W-4 Instructions; FLSA

description: The worker's federal or state tax filing status as declared on the withholding form. Drives the applicable standard deduction and tax bracket used in withholding calculations. Values align with IRS filing status categories.
reference: IRS W-4; IRS Publication 15-T; IRS Publication 501

description: Fixed percentage rate applied to gross wages for income tax withholding when the withholding method is 'percentage' or 'flat_amount'. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.2200 = 22%). Used for supplemental wage withholding at the IRS flat supplemental rate or for state flat-rate withholding.
reference: IRS Publication 15-T Supplemental Wage Withholding; TempWorks Payroll

description: The specific tax withholding form type submitted by the worker. Examples include W-4 (federal), W-4P (pension), state equivalents (e.g., CA DE-4, NY IT-2104, IL W-4, TX no state income tax). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: W-4|W-4P|W-4S|W-4V|DE-4|IT-2104|IL-W-4|VA-4|NC-4|GA-G-4 — promote to reference product]
reference: IRS W-4; IRS Publication 15-T; State Revenue Agencies

description: The maximum number of withholding allowances permitted by the IRS lock-in letter, overriding the worker's own W-4 election. Employer must not allow the worker to claim more allowances than this value.
reference: IRS Publication 15-T; IRS Lock-In Letter Program

description: The filing status mandated by the IRS lock-in letter, overriding the worker's own W-4 election. Populated only when an IRS lock-in letter is in effect. Employer must use this status for withholding calculations.
reference: IRS Publication 15-T; IRS Lock-In Letter Program

description: Date of the IRS lock-in letter received by the employer mandating a specific withholding rate for this worker. When present, the employer must withhold at the IRS-specified rate regardless of the worker's W-4 elections. Null if no lock-in letter applies.
reference: IRS Publication 15-T; IRS Lock-In Letter Program; IRS Notice 2017-67

description: Indicates whether the worker has claimed exemption from federal or state income tax withholding. True = worker claims exempt status and no income tax will be withheld. Exempt status expires February 15 each year and must be renewed. Employer must retain the exempt W-4 and notify IRS if required.
reference: IRS W-4 Exempt Status; IRS Publication 15-T; IRS Notice 2018-92

description: Indicates whether the worker has claimed exemption from state income tax withholding on the state withholding form. Exempt criteria and renewal requirements vary by state.
reference: State Revenue Agencies; TempWorks Payroll Multi-State Payroll

description: Indicates whether this election applies to federal, state, or local tax withholding. Federal elections are governed by IRS W-4; state elections by equivalent state withholding forms; local elections by municipality-specific forms.
reference: IRS Publication 15-T; U.S. Department of Labor (DOL); FLSA

description: Name of the local taxing jurisdiction (city, county, or municipality) for local income tax withholding elections. Applicable in states with local income taxes such as Ohio, Pennsylvania, Kentucky, and New York City.
reference: TempWorks Payroll Multi-State Payroll; U.S. Department of Labor (DOL)

description: Indicates whether the worker checked the Step 2 multiple jobs checkbox on the 2020+ W-4, signaling they hold multiple concurrent jobs or their spouse also works. When true, withholding is calculated using the higher withholding rate tables to prevent under-withholding.
reference: IRS W-4 Step 2 (2020+); IRS Publication 15-T

description: Indicates whether the worker is a nonresident alien (NRA) for U.S. tax purposes. NRA workers are subject to special withholding rules under IRS Publication 15 and must follow specific W-4 instructions (cannot claim exempt, must add an additional amount to wages for withholding calculation). Relevant for staffing firms placing international workers.
reference: IRS Publication 15; IRS Publication 515; Immigration and Nationality Act (INA); IRS W-4 NRA Instructions

description: Dollar amount of other non-wage income (interest, dividends, retirement income) entered in Step 4a of the 2020+ W-4. Increases withholding to cover tax on non-wage income. Null for pre-2020 W-4 forms.
reference: IRS W-4 Step 4a (2020+); IRS Publication 15-T

description: The pay frequency associated with this withholding election, used to annualize wages for withholding table lookups. Must match the worker's actual pay frequency in the pay run. Drives the correct withholding amount per period.
reference: IRS Publication 15-T; TempWorks Payroll Pay Frequency Configuration

description: Date the withholding election form was received by the employer or payroll department. Used to determine the required effective date per IRS rules (must take effect no later than the first payroll period ending on or after the 30th day after receipt).
reference: IRS Publication 15-T; IRS W-4 Instructions

description: Additional flat dollar amount the worker requests to be withheld for state income tax beyond the calculated state withholding. Applied per pay period in addition to the standard state withholding calculation.
reference: State Revenue Agencies; TempWorks Payroll Multi-State Payroll

description: Number of withholding allowances claimed on the state withholding form. Many states still use an allowance-based system independent of the federal W-4 redesign (e.g., California DE-4, New York IT-2104). Null for states with no income tax or states that have adopted the federal W-4.
reference: State Revenue Agencies; TempWorks Payroll Multi-State Payroll

description: Two-letter USPS state abbreviation identifying the state jurisdiction for state or local withholding elections. Null for federal elections. Supports multi-state payroll compliance across all states where Staffing Hr places workers.
reference: USPS State Abbreviations; SUTA (State Unemployment Tax Act); TempWorks Payroll Multi-State Payroll

description: The worker's filing status as declared on the state withholding form, which may differ from the federal filing status. State-specific values vary by jurisdiction (e.g., California uses single, married, head of household with different withholding tables). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: single|married|married_higher_rate|head_of_household|exempt — promote to reference product]
reference: State Revenue Agencies; TempWorks Payroll Multi-State Payroll; SUTA

description: Method used to withhold income tax on supplemental wages (bonuses, commissions, overtime, per diem above IRS threshold). Flat rate = mandatory 22% federal flat rate for supplemental wages under $1M; Aggregate = combined with regular wages using withholding tables; Optional flat = employer elects flat rate when not mandatory.
reference: IRS Publication 15-T Supplemental Wages; IRS Revenue Ruling 2008-29

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country with which the worker claims a U.S. tax treaty benefit, potentially reducing or eliminating withholding on certain income types. Applicable for nonresident alien workers claiming treaty exemptions via Form 8233 or W-8BEN.
reference: IRS Publication 515; IRS Form 8233; IRS Form W-8BEN; U.S. Tax Treaties

description: Timestamp when this withholding election record was last modified. Tracks changes to election data for audit trail and data lineage purposes in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: SOC 2 Type II; TempWorks Payroll Audit Trail; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

description: The tax year version of the W-4 or equivalent withholding form submitted by the worker. Critical because the 2020 redesigned W-4 eliminated allowances and introduced a new step-based structure. Pre-2020 forms use allowances; 2020+ forms use Step 3 dependent credits and Step 4 adjustments.
reference: IRS W-4 (2020 Redesign); IRS Publication 15-T

description: The calculation method used to compute income tax withholding for this worker. Percentage method uses IRS Publication 15-T tables; Wage bracket method uses bracket tables; Flat amount applies a fixed dollar amount; Annualized projects annual income for withholding; Cumulative adjusts for year-to-date withholding.
reference: IRS Publication 15-T Withholding Methods; TempWorks Payroll

description: Classification of the worker for tax withholding purposes. W-2 = employee subject to income tax withholding and FICA; 1099 = independent contractor (IC) not subject to employer withholding; EOR = Employer of Record arrangement where the EOR entity handles withholding. Drives whether withholding elections are applicable.
reference: IRS Worker Classification Rules; IRS Publication 15; IRS Form 1099; W-2 (Wage and Tax Statement); 1099 (Independent Contractor Tax Form); EOR (Employer of Record)

description: The total employer-side cost loading rate applied on top of the pay rate, expressed as a decimal percentage. Encompasses FICA, FUTA, SUTA, workers compensation, and benefits costs. Used in true cost-of-labor calculations.
reference: IRS FICA Regulations; FUTA (Federal Unemployment Tax Act); SUTA (State Unemployment Tax Act); TempWorks Payroll

description: The one-time fee charged to the client when a temporary or contract-to-hire worker is converted to a permanent employee. Defined in the client MSA and applicable only for temp-to-perm placement types.
reference: DocuSign CLM MSA Management; ASA Temp-to-Perm Conversion Standards; Salesforce Revenue Cloud

description: The date and time when this rate record was first created in the system. Provides the foundational audit trail entry for data lineage, compliance, and record lifecycle tracking.
reference: SOC 2 Type II Audit Controls; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); CCPA

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code applicable to all monetary rate fields in this record (e.g., USD, CAD). Supports multi-currency operations for international staffing engagements.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; Oracle NetSuite ERP General Ledger

description: The percentage of the placed candidate's first-year annual salary charged as the direct hire placement fee. Applicable only for direct hire and permanent placement engagements. Defined in the client MSA.
reference: DocuSign CLM MSA Management; ASA Direct Placement Fee Standards; Salesforce Revenue Cloud

description: The hourly bill rate charged to the client for double-time hours, typically applicable on holidays or after extended daily thresholds per client contract or state law. Used in client invoicing for DT hours.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); State Labor Laws; Bullhorn ATS/CRM

description: The hourly pay rate for double-time hours, typically 2x the regular pay rate. Applicable per client contract terms or state-mandated double-time rules. Used in payroll processing for DT-eligible hours.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); State Labor Laws; TempWorks Payroll

description: The date on which this rate record becomes active and applicable to payroll and billing calculations. Marks the start of the rate's binding period for the associated placement.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); ASA Staffing Industry Standards

description: The date on which this rate record ceases to be applicable. Null indicates an open-ended rate with no defined end. Used to manage rate versioning, extensions, and contract renewals.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM; Beeline VMS Rate Management

description: The gross margin expressed as a percentage of the bill rate, calculated as (Spread / Bill Rate). Represents the profitability ratio for this rate record and is a primary KPI for financial reporting and account management.
reference: ASA Staffing Industry Financial Standards; Staffing Industry Analysts (SIA); Oracle NetSuite ERP Revenue Recognition

business_glossary_term: IRS GSA (General Services Administration) Rate Reference
description: The IRS General Services Administration (GSA) per diem rate reference code or location identifier used to validate per diem allowances against federally published rates. Applicable for per_diem rate types to ensure IRS compliance.
reference: IRS GSA Per Diem Rate Schedule; IRS Publication 463; OFCCP Compliance

description: The hourly bill rate charged to the client for hours worked on designated holidays. Defined in the client MSA or SOW and used in holiday billing calculations.
reference: DocuSign CLM MSA Management; Bullhorn ATS/CRM; Salesforce Revenue Cloud

description: The hourly pay rate for hours worked on designated holidays. Defined in the worker's assignment terms and used in payroll processing for holiday-worked hours.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); TempWorks Payroll; ASA Holiday Pay Guidelines

description: Indicates whether this rate record is currently active and eligible for use in payroll and billing calculations. A rate may be inactive due to expiration, supersession by a newer rate version, or manual deactivation.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM; Beeline VMS Rate Management; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: Indicates whether this rate or per diem allowance is subject to federal and state income tax withholding. Per diem amounts at or below GSA rates are typically non-taxable; amounts exceeding GSA rates are taxable as wages.
reference: IRS Publication 463; IRS GSA Per Diem Rate Schedule; FICA Regulations; TempWorks Payroll Tax Filing

description: The occupational classification code (e.g., DOL SOC code or client-defined job category code) associated with this rate. Drives workers compensation rate assignment, FLSA exemption status, and rate card categorization.
reference: DOL Standard Occupational Classification (SOC); FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); OSHA; TempWorks Payroll

description: The percentage markup applied over the pay rate to derive the bill rate, expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 0.35 = 35%). Used in rate negotiations, client proposals, and margin analysis reporting.
reference: ASA Staffing Industry Financial Standards; Staffing Industry Analysts (SIA)

description: Free-text field for capturing additional context, negotiation history, special conditions, or exceptions associated with this rate record. Used by account managers and recruiters to document rate-specific business decisions.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: The hourly bill rate charged to the client for overtime hours worked beyond the standard threshold (typically 40 hours/week under FLSA). Distinct from the standard bill rate to support accurate client invoicing for OT hours.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); Bullhorn ATS/CRM; Salesforce Revenue Cloud

description: The hourly pay rate for overtime hours, required to be at least 1.5x the regular pay rate under FLSA. Used in payroll processing for hours exceeding the standard weekly threshold.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); DOL Wage and Hour Division; TempWorks Payroll

description: The hourly or unit rate paid to the worker for services rendered. Represents the worker-facing compensation component used in payroll processing. Must comply with applicable minimum wage laws under FLSA.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); TempWorks Payroll; DOL Wage and Hour Division

description: The maximum total per diem budget authorized for this rate record over the assignment period. Used to enforce spending controls and flag overages in per diem reimbursement processing.
reference: IRS GSA Per Diem Rate Schedule; Internal Per Diem Policy; TempWorks Payroll

description: Sub-classification of per diem rate type indicating the specific allowance category. Applicable only when rate_type = 'per_diem'. Aligns with IRS GSA per diem schedule categories for tax compliance and reimbursement tracking.
reference: IRS GSA Per Diem Rate Schedule; IRS Publication 463; TempWorks Payroll Per Diem Configuration

description: The approved daily monetary allowance for the per diem category (travel, lodging, meals, or incidentals). Represents the maximum reimbursable or taxable daily amount for the applicable per diem category.
reference: IRS GSA Per Diem Rate Schedule; IRS Publication 463; TempWorks Payroll Per Diem Configuration

description: The type of placement engagement this rate record supports. Temporary covers standard temp assignments; contract_to_hire (temp-to-perm) includes conversion terms; direct_hire covers permanent placement fees; SOW (Statement of Work) covers project-based engagements.
reference: ASA Staffing Industry Standards; Bullhorn ATS/CRM Placement Object; Beeline VMS

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this rate record within the source system (Bullhorn, Beeline VMS, or TempWorks). Used for cross-system reconciliation and rate card referencing.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM; Beeline VMS Rate Management; TempWorks Payroll

description: The originating system or method from which this rate record was sourced. Bullhorn indicates the ATS rate card; beeline_vms indicates the VMS rate management module; tempworks indicates the payroll per diem configuration; manual indicates a directly entered rate.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM; Beeline VMS Rate Management; TempWorks Payroll

description: Classification of the rate component this record represents. Standard covers regular bill/pay rates; overtime (OT) and double-time (DT) apply to FLSA-governed hours; holiday covers premium holiday pay; per_diem covers travel/lodging/meals/incidentals allowances; burden covers employer-side cost loading. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: standard|overtime|double_time|holiday|per_diem|burden — promote to reference product if additional types emerge]
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); IRS GSA Per Diem Guidelines; American Staffing Association (ASA)

description: The method used to calculate and process per diem reimbursements. Actual expense requires receipts; flat_rate pays a fixed daily amount regardless of actual spend; gsa_rate uses the IRS GSA published rate for the work location.
reference: IRS Publication 463; IRS GSA Per Diem Rate Schedule; TempWorks Payroll

description: The gross dollar difference between the bill rate and the pay rate (Bill Rate minus Pay Rate). Represents the staffing firm's gross revenue per hour before burden costs. A key profitability metric tracked at the placement level.
reference: ASA Staffing Industry Financial Standards; Staffing Industry Analysts (SIA)

description: The time or work unit basis for the bill and pay rates. Hourly is standard for temporary staffing; daily/weekly/monthly may apply to contract or SOW engagements; fixed applies to direct hire placement fees.
reference: ASA Staffing Industry Standards; Bullhorn ATS/CRM; Beeline VMS Rate Management

description: The date and time when this rate record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, data synchronization across systems, and audit compliance.
reference: SOC 2 Type II Audit Controls; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); CCPA

description: Sequential version number for this rate record, incremented each time the rate is renegotiated or updated. Supports rate versioning and historical rate tracking for audit and analytics purposes.
reference: Internal Rate Governance Policy; SOC 2 Type II Audit Controls

description: The external rate identifier assigned by the Beeline VMS system for this rate record. Used for cross-system reconciliation between the staffing firm's internal systems and the client's VMS program.
reference: Beeline VMS Rate Management; VMS Integration Standards

description: Two-letter US state code for the state where the work is performed. Determines applicable SUTA rate, state minimum wage compliance, workers compensation jurisdiction, and state income tax withholding rules.
reference: SUTA (State Unemployment Tax Act); DOL Wage and Hour Division; State Workers Compensation Boards; IRS

description: The workers compensation insurance rate applied to this placement, expressed as a decimal percentage of payroll. Varies by job classification code and state. Used in burden rate calculation and insurance cost allocation.
reference: OSHA; State Workers Compensation Boards; TempWorks Payroll Workers Compensation Module

description: Unique system-generated identifier for each redeployment event record. Primary key for the redeployment data product within the placement domain. reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the internal recruiter or staffing coordinator responsible for managing this redeployment event and driving the worker back to active placement.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM User Object; ASA Workforce Management Standards

description: Foreign key linking to recruitment.submittal. Business justification: Redeployment candidates reference original submittal for skills verification, client preference history, and prior RTR agreements. Essential for bench management and rapid redeployment to similar role
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the client account being targeted for the worker's next placement during the redeployment process. Null until a specific client opportunity is identified.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Client Object

description: Reference to the new placement record created as the successful outcome of this redeployment event. Null until the worker is successfully redeployed to a new assignment.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Placement Object

reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Placement Object; FLSA Assignment Tracking

description: The date on which the candidate becomes fully available for a new assignment. May differ from assignment_end_date due to notice periods, PTO, or contractual obligations. Critical input for redeployment scheduling and coordinator outreach.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Candidate Availability; ASA Workforce Management Standards

description: Estimated financial exposure (in pay_rate_currency) associated with the worker remaining on bench, calculated as the worker's pay rate multiplied by projected bench days. Stored as a point-in-time snapshot for financial risk reporting. Confidential financial data.
reference: Oracle NetSuite ERP Financial Reporting; SIA Workforce Analytics; Power BI KPI Dashboards

description: Fee charged to the client when a temporary worker is converted to a permanent hire (temp-to-perm conversion). Applicable when redeployment_type is 'temp_to_perm'. Confidential financial data tied to the MSA/contract terms.
reference: Salesforce Revenue Cloud Billing; MSA Contract Terms; ASA Conversion Fee Standards

description: The timestamp when this redeployment record was first created in the system. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED field for the TRANSACTION_HEADER role. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: SOC 2 Type II Audit Trail Requirements; GDPR Article 5 Data Integrity

description: Number of client interviews the worker attended during this redeployment event. Used to measure conversion rate from submittal to interview and assess redeployment pipeline health.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Interview Tracking; SIA Workforce Analytics

description: Indicates whether this redeployment event is associated with a backfill scenario, where the worker is being redeployed to replace another departing worker at the same or different client site.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Placement Backfill Tracking; ASA Workforce Management Standards

description: The most recent date on which the coordinator made contact or attempted contact with the worker regarding redeployment opportunities. Used to identify stale redeployment records requiring follow-up.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Activity Tracking; ASA Bench Management Standards

description: Free-text coordinator notes capturing context, candidate preferences, client feedback, or special circumstances relevant to this redeployment event. Supports qualitative tracking alongside structured fields.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Activity Notes

description: Final disposition of the redeployment event. 'redeployed' = placed on new assignment; 'converted' = temp-to-perm conversion; 'separated' = worker left the workforce pool; 'extended' = original assignment extended; 'declined' = worker declined available opportunities; 'no_show' = worker became unresponsive.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Redeployment Workflow; ASA Fall-off Rate Standards; SIA Workforce Analytics

description: Count of coordinator contact attempts made to the worker during the redeployment process (calls, emails, texts). Used to measure engagement effort and trigger escalation workflows when thresholds are exceeded.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Activity Tracking; ASA Bench Management Standards

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the pay rate fields (e.g., USD). Supports multi-currency operations for international staffing engagements.

description: The minimum hourly or salary pay rate the worker is willing to accept for a new assignment. Used by coordinators to filter job orders and negotiate placements during redeployment. Confidential business data.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Candidate Pay Expectations; FLSA Minimum Wage Standards

description: The worker's preferred geographic area or city/state for their next assignment. Free-text or structured location string used by coordinators to filter and match available job orders during redeployment outreach.

description: Two-letter US state code representing the worker's preferred state for redeployment. Used for geographic filtering in job order matching and workforce planning analytics.

description: The worker's stated preference for the type of engagement on their next assignment. Guides coordinator matching and job order targeting during the redeployment process.

description: The worker's primary professional skill or job title used as the lead matching criterion during redeployment job order search. Sourced from the candidate profile in Bullhorn ATS.

description: Coordinator-assigned urgency level for this redeployment event. 'critical' = worker at risk of separation or has specialized skills in high demand; 'high' = near-term bench cost risk; 'medium' = standard pipeline; 'low' = worker has indicated flexibility or is not immediately available.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Redeployment Workflow; ASA Bench Management Standards

description: Externally-visible business identifier for this redeployment event, used in coordinator workflows, reporting, and communications. Format: RDP- followed by 7 digits. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for the TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Redeployment Workflow; ASA Bench Management Standards

description: Indicates how this redeployment record was created. 'bullhorn_workflow' = auto-generated by Bullhorn redeployment workflow trigger; 'manual_entry' = coordinator manually created; 'vms_notification' = triggered by Beeline VMS assignment end notification; 'coordinator_initiated' = proactive coordinator action; 'system_auto' = automated rule-based creation.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Redeployment Workflow; Beeline VMS Integration

description: Current lifecycle state of the redeployment event. 'bench' = worker is unassigned and available; 'in_process' = active outreach and submittal activity underway; 'redeployed' = successfully placed on a new assignment; 'converted' = temp-to-perm conversion occurred; 'separated' = worker exited the workforce pool. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS for the TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Redeployment Workflow; ASA Staffing Industry Standards; SIA Workforce Analytics

description: Classification of the redeployment pathway. 'internal_transfer' = moved to another assignment within same client; 'new_client' = placed with a different client; 'temp_to_perm' = converted to permanent hire; 'contract_extension' = existing assignment extended; 'reactivation' = previously separated worker re-engaged.

description: The number of overtime hours specifically contested within the dispute. Relevant for unauthorized_ot dispute types where the client or back-office challenges OT hours that were not pre-approved. Governed by FLSA overtime provisions.
reference: FLSA — Overtime Provisions (29 CFR Part 778); Kronos Workforce Ready

description: The worker's hourly pay rate applicable to the disputed timesheet period. Used to calculate the payable adjustment amount for the worker. Sourced from TempWorks Payroll and the placement record.
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Rate Management; FLSA — Minimum Wage and Overtime; DOL

description: The per diem reimbursement amount being contested in the dispute. Applicable when dispute_type is per_diem_dispute. Per diem rates are governed by IRS guidelines and client MSA terms.
reference: IRS Publication 463 — Per Diem Rates; DOL; Placement MSA Terms

description: The number of previously submitted disputes associated with the same worker and placement at the time this dispute was raised. Used for risk flagging, pattern detection, and compliance reporting. A high count may indicate a systemic timekeeping issue.
reference: ASA Best Practices — Risk Management; Power BI Analytics Platform — Workforce Analytics

description: The number of hours as originally recorded on the timesheet at the time the dispute was raised. Provides the baseline for comparison against the worker's or client's claimed hours.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready — Time and Attendance; FLSA 29 CFR Part 516

description: The calendar date on which the dispute was formally resolved and a resolution_outcome was recorded. Used to calculate actual resolution cycle time against SLA targets.
reference: ASA SLA Standards; Kronos Workforce Ready — Dispute Management

description: Free-text narrative documenting the findings, evidence reviewed, and rationale for the resolution outcome. Captured by the resolving party and retained for compliance and audit purposes.
reference: SOC 2 Type II — Audit Trail; ASA Recordkeeping Standards; FCRA

description: The final determination of the dispute. Values: approved_in_full (all disputed hours/amounts accepted), approved_partial (partial adjustment granted), denied (dispute rejected), withdrawn (initiator retracted before resolution), no_action_required (investigation found no discrepancy). Null while dispute is open or under review.
reference: ASA Best Practices — Dispute Resolution; Kronos Workforce Ready

description: The final monetary adjustment amount approved as a result of the dispute resolution. Drives payroll correction entries in TempWorks and billing adjustments in Salesforce Revenue Cloud. Null until resolution_outcome is set.
reference: TempWorks Payroll; Salesforce Revenue Cloud — Credit Memo; Oracle NetSuite ERP

description: The final agreed-upon number of hours after dispute resolution. May equal claimed_hours (full approval), a value between recorded_hours and claimed_hours (partial), or recorded_hours (denial). Used to drive payroll and billing adjustments.
reference: TempWorks Payroll — Adjustment Processing; Salesforce Revenue Cloud

description: The internal role or team currently responsible for investigating and resolving the dispute. Used for workload assignment, SLA accountability, and escalation routing. Values: staffing_coordinator, payroll_team, client_manager, vms_admin, escalation_team.
reference: ASA Best Practices — Dispute Ownership; Kronos Workforce Ready

description: Indicates whether the dispute resolution exceeded the defined SLA target hours. True when the dispute was not resolved within sla_target_hours of submitted_timestamp. Feeds SLA compliance reporting and client KPI dashboards.
reference: ASA SLA Standards; MSA Terms; Power BI Analytics Platform — KPI Dashboards

business_glossary_term: Service Level Agreement (SLA) Target Resolution Hours
description: The contractually or operationally defined number of business hours within which the dispute must be resolved. Sourced from the client MSA or internal SLA policy. Used to calculate SLA compliance and breach status.
reference: ASA SLA Standards; MSA Terms; DOL — Timely Payment Requirements

description: The channel through which the dispute was submitted. Values: portal (worker or client self-service portal), email (submitted via email to back-office), phone (verbal submission logged by coordinator), vms (raised through Beeline VMS), ats (raised through Bullhorn ATS/CRM), manual (back-office data entry). Used for channel analytics and process improvement.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready; Beeline VMS; Bullhorn ATS/CRM

description: The exact date and time when the dispute was formally submitted into the system. This is the principal business event timestamp used as the SLA clock start for dispute resolution tracking.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready — Dispute Management; ASA SLA Standards

description: Indicates whether supporting documentation (e.g., badge swipe records, supervisor sign-off, email correspondence, system logs) has been attached to the dispute record. True when at least one document has been submitted as evidence.
reference: SOC 2 Type II — Evidence Management; FCRA; ASA Recordkeeping Standards

description: The week-ending date of the pay period associated with the disputed timesheet. Used to align the dispute with the correct payroll cycle and billing period for adjustment processing.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready — Pay Period Management; TempWorks Payroll

description: The dispute or ticket reference number assigned by the client's VMS platform (e.g., Beeline) when the dispute was raised through a managed service program. Enables cross-system traceability for MSP/VMS-managed accounts. Null for non-VMS clients.
reference: Beeline VMS — Dispute Management; MSP Program Standards

business_glossary_term: Vendor Management System (VMS) Timesheet Sync ID
description: Unique surrogate primary key for each VMS timesheet synchronization record in the Staffing Hr lakehouse Silver layer. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — represents a discrete sync event with its own lifecycle between Kronos Workforce Ready and a client VMS platform.
reference: Staffing Hr Data Modeling Standards; ASA Data Governance Framework

description: Reference to the contingent worker placement record associated with this timesheet sync. Identifies the specific assignment under which the worker submitted hours, linking the sync event to the placement lifecycle in Bullhorn ATS/CRM.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Placement Module; ASA Staffing Industry Standards

description: Reference to the client organization whose VMS platform is the target or source of this synchronization. Identifies the MSP/VMS-managed program client for billing dispute resolution and program reporting.
reference: Bullhorn ATS/CRM Client Module; Beeline VMS Client Configuration

description: Foreign key linking to client.managed_program. Business justification: VMS sync occurs within managed programs (MSP/RPO); program-specific integration rules and SLA tracking require this link. Essential for managed program performance reporting and program-specific VMS r
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the contingent worker whose timesheet hours are being synchronized. Enables worker-level reconciliation reporting and audit trails for payroll and billing accuracy.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready Worker Profile; Bullhorn ATS/CRM Candidate Module

description: Reference to the internal Kronos Workforce Ready timesheet record being synchronized. Links this sync event to the authoritative timesheet in the internal time-and-attendance system.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready Time and Attendance Module; ASA Workforce Data Standards

description: Foreign key linking to vendor.vms_enrollment. Business justification: VMS timesheet synchronization requires vendor enrollment context to route data correctly to VMS platforms (Fieldglass, Beeline). Integration middleware must identify which vendor enrollment applies to
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: The identifier of the MSP/VMS-managed contingent workforce program within the VMS platform. Used to segment sync records by client program for program-level reporting, SLA tracking, and billing reconciliation under MSP agreements.
reference: Beeline VMS Program Configuration; SIA MSP Program Standards; ASA MSP/VMS Program Guidelines

description: The approval state of the timesheet within the client VMS platform. 'pending' = awaiting client manager approval; 'approved' = client approved in VMS; 'rejected' = client rejected in VMS; 'disputed' = under active dispute; 'recalled' = previously approved but recalled for correction. Drives billing eligibility.
reference: Beeline VMS Approval Workflow; SIA VMS Data Standards; ASA Client Billing Standards

description: The hourly bill rate applied to this timesheet for client invoicing purposes, as agreed in the MSA or VMS rate card. Used to validate that the rate applied in the VMS matches the contracted rate in Kronos/Bullhorn. A mismatch triggers a billing dispute.
reference: Beeline VMS Rate Management; Salesforce Revenue Cloud Billing; ASA Staffing Industry Standards; MSA Rate Schedule

description: The client cost center code associated with this timesheet as recorded in the VMS platform. Used for client-side labor cost allocation and is a common source of field-level mapping discrepancies between Kronos and VMS systems.
reference: Oracle NetSuite ERP General Ledger; Beeline VMS Cost Center Configuration; ASA Client Billing Standards

description: The date and time when this VMS timesheet sync record was first created in the Staffing Hr lakehouse. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED timestamp for data lineage and audit trail purposes.
reference: SOC 2 Type II Audit Requirements; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); ASA Data Governance Framework

description: Total double-time (DT) hours recorded on the timesheet being synchronized, applicable in states such as California where DT is mandated for hours beyond 12 in a day or 8 on the 7th consecutive day. Ensures accurate billing and payroll at DT rates.
reference: California Labor Code Section 510; FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); DOL Wage and Hour Division; Kronos Workforce Ready OT Rules Engine

description: The error code returned by the VMS platform or integration middleware when a sync attempt fails or is rejected. Used for automated error classification, retry logic routing, and integration support triage. Null when sync_status is 'synced'.
reference: Beeline VMS API Error Code Reference; Kronos Workforce Ready Integration Error Catalog; ASA Technology Standards

description: Human-readable error description returned by the VMS platform or integration layer when a sync fails or is rejected. Provides context for manual investigation and resolution of failed sync events. Null when sync_status is 'synced'.
reference: Beeline VMS API Documentation; Kronos Workforce Ready Integration Guide; SOC 2 Type II Incident Management

description: A structured description of specific field-level mismatches identified between the Kronos Workforce Ready timesheet and the VMS timesheet record (e.g., cost center code mismatch, job code mismatch, worker ID format difference). Stored as a delimited string of field names with discrepancy details. Used for root-cause analysis and integration mapping corrections.
reference: Beeline VMS Field Mapping Specification; Kronos Workforce Ready Data Dictionary; ASA Data Governance Framework

description: The difference between vms_total_hours and total_hours (VMS hours minus Kronos hours). A non-zero value indicates a discrepancy requiring reconciliation. Positive values mean the VMS recorded more hours; negative values mean Kronos recorded more hours. Used to prioritize reconciliation effort and assess billing risk.
reference: ASA Billing Dispute Resolution Guidelines; Beeline VMS Reconciliation Specification; SIA VMS Data Standards

description: The batch or job run identifier from the integration middleware that processed this sync record. Used for operational troubleshooting, replay of failed batches, and integration audit trails. Distinct from internal ETL metadata — this is a business-visible integration reference used by the integration operations team.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready Integration Middleware; Beeline VMS API Batch Processing; SOC 2 Type II Availability Controls

business_glossary_term: Kronos Workforce Ready Timesheet Reference ID
description: The internal timesheet identifier as assigned by Kronos Workforce Ready. Used to cross-reference the internal time-and-attendance record with the VMS record during reconciliation and audit.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready Time and Attendance Module; ASA Workforce Data Standards

description: The date and time of the most recent retry attempt for this synchronization record. Used alongside retry_count to calculate retry intervals, enforce exponential backoff policies, and identify stale failed syncs requiring manual intervention.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready Integration Retry Policy; Beeline VMS API Documentation; SOC 2 Type II Availability Controls

description: The username or employee identifier of the Staffing Hr operator who applied the manual override to this sync record. Required for SOC 2 audit trail and accountability. Populated only when manual_override_flag is True.
reference: SOC 2 Type II Access Control Requirements; GDPR Article 5 (Accountability); Staffing Hr Internal Audit Policy

description: Indicates whether a human operator manually overrode the automated sync result for this record (True = manual override applied; False = automated sync result). Manual overrides are required when automated reconciliation cannot resolve discrepancies. Triggers enhanced audit logging per SOC 2 controls.
reference: SOC 2 Type II Change Management Controls; ASA Data Governance Framework; Staffing Hr Internal Audit Policy

description: Free-text explanation provided by the operator when a manual override is applied to this sync record. Required when manual_override_flag is True. Documents the business justification for the override for audit and compliance purposes.
reference: SOC 2 Type II Change Management Controls; ASA Data Governance Framework; Staffing Hr Internal Audit Policy

description: Total overtime (OT) hours recorded on the timesheet being synchronized, typically hours worked beyond 40 per week or 8 per day per FLSA or applicable state law. Critical for accurate billing at OT bill rates and worker compensation at OT pay rates.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act) Section 7; DOL Wage and Hour Division; Kronos Workforce Ready OT Rules Engine

description: The hourly pay rate for the contingent worker associated with this timesheet, as recorded in the payroll system. Used alongside bill_rate to calculate spread and gross margin. Confidential compensation data.
reference: TempWorks Payroll Pay Rate Configuration; FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act) Minimum Wage Requirements; DOL Wage and Hour Division

description: The per diem (daily expense allowance) amount included in this timesheet record, if applicable. Per diem is a non-taxable reimbursement for meals and incidentals for workers on travel assignments. Must be reconciled between Kronos and VMS to ensure accurate billing and payroll.
reference: IRS Publication 463 (Travel Expenses); DOL Per Diem Regulations; ASA Staffing Industry Standards

description: The final outcome of the reconciliation process for this sync record. 'matched' = hours match exactly with no intervention; 'reconciled' = discrepancy resolved through manual or automated correction; 'unresolved' = discrepancy remains open; 'escalated' = referred to billing dispute team; 'voided' = timesheet voided and excluded from billing. Critical for billing dispute management and MSP program reporting.
reference: ASA Billing Dispute Resolution Guidelines; Beeline VMS Reconciliation Workflow; SIA MSP Program Standards

description: The date and time when the reconciliation outcome was determined and recorded for this sync record. Used for SLA measurement of reconciliation cycle time and billing cutoff compliance.
reference: ASA Billing Dispute Resolution Guidelines; Beeline VMS Reconciliation Workflow; SIA SLA Reporting Standards

description: Total regular (straight-time) hours recorded on the timesheet being synchronized. Used to verify that regular hours match between Kronos Workforce Ready and the VMS platform to prevent billing disputes.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act); DOL Wage and Hour Division; Kronos Workforce Ready Time and Attendance Module

description: The number of times this synchronization has been retried after an initial failure. Used to enforce maximum retry thresholds, trigger escalation workflows, and measure integration reliability. A high retry count may indicate a systemic VMS connectivity or data mapping issue.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready Integration Retry Policy; Beeline VMS SLA Requirements; ASA Technology Standards

description: Indicates the direction of the timesheet data flow: 'push' means Kronos Workforce Ready is sending hours to the VMS, 'pull' means the VMS-approved timesheet is being retrieved into Kronos. Determines the authoritative source for reconciliation.
reference: Beeline VMS Integration Specification; Kronos Workforce Ready API Documentation; ASA Technology Standards

description: Current lifecycle state of this timesheet synchronization attempt. 'pending' = awaiting processing; 'synced' = successfully matched in both systems; 'failed' = technical error prevented sync; 'rejected' = VMS rejected the timesheet data; 'partial' = some fields synced but discrepancies remain. This is the LIFECYCLE_STATUS for the sync transaction.
reference: Beeline VMS Integration Specification; Kronos Workforce Ready API Documentation; ASA Data Governance Framework

description: The date and time when this synchronization attempt was executed. Represents the BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP — the principal real-world event time of the sync operation. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready API Documentation; Beeline VMS Integration Specification; ISO 8601

description: Identifies the authoritative source system from which the timesheet data originated for this sync event. 'Kronos' = Kronos Workforce Ready is the source of record; 'VMS' = the client VMS platform is the source of record (pull scenario); 'Manual' = hours were entered manually outside of either system. Used for data lineage and audit.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready Data Governance; Beeline VMS Integration Specification; ASA Data Governance Framework

description: Total billable hours on the timesheet (sum of regular, OT, and DT hours) as recorded in the source system. Used as the primary reconciliation figure between Kronos Workforce Ready and the VMS platform. Discrepancies in this field trigger billing dispute workflows.
reference: ASA Staffing Industry Standards; Beeline VMS Timesheet Reconciliation; Kronos Workforce Ready Time and Attendance Module

description: The date and time when this VMS timesheet sync record was last modified, such as after a retry, manual override, or reconciliation outcome update. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED timestamp.
reference: SOC 2 Type II Audit Requirements; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); ASA Data Governance Framework

description: The date and time when the client manager approved the timesheet within the VMS platform. Marks the point at which hours become billable and payable. Used for Time-to-Approve (TTA) SLA reporting and billing cycle cutoff determination.
reference: Beeline VMS Approval Workflow; SIA SLA Reporting Standards; ASA Client Billing Standards

description: The name of the client manager or supervisor who approved or rejected the timesheet within the VMS platform. Required for audit trail, dispute resolution, and SLA compliance reporting under MSP/VMS program agreements.
reference: Beeline VMS Approval Workflow; SOC 2 Type II Audit Requirements; ASA MSP Program Standards

business_glossary_term: Vendor Management System (VMS) Job Reference ID
description: The job or requisition identifier as assigned by the client VMS platform. Used to associate the synced timesheet with the correct VMS job order or requisition for cost center allocation and client billing.
reference: Beeline VMS Job Order Module; SAP Fieldglass Requisition Module; SIA VMS Data Standards

description: Name of the client Vendor Management System (VMS) platform involved in this synchronization event. Identifies whether the sync is with Beeline, SAP Fieldglass, VNDLY, Coupa, Workday, or another VMS. Critical for platform-specific error handling and integration routing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Beeline|Fieldglass|VNDLY|Coupa|Workday|Other — promote to reference product if additional platforms are onboarded]
reference: Beeline VMS Integration Specification; SIA VMS Market Report; ASA Technology Standards

business_glossary_term: Vendor Management System (VMS) Timesheet Reference ID
description: The external timesheet identifier assigned by the client VMS platform (e.g., Beeline timesheet number, Fieldglass time sheet ID). Used for cross-system reconciliation and billing dispute resolution. This is the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for the sync transaction as known externally.
reference: Beeline VMS API Specification; SAP Fieldglass Integration Guide; SIA VMS Data Standards

description: Total hours as recorded or approved within the client VMS platform for this timesheet period. Compared against total_hours from Kronos to identify discrepancies. A mismatch between this field and total_hours is the primary trigger for reconciliation workflows and billing dispute escalation.
reference: Beeline VMS Timesheet Approval Workflow; SIA VMS Data Standards; ASA Billing Dispute Resolution Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Vendor Management System (VMS) Worker Reference ID
description: The worker identifier as assigned by the client VMS platform (e.g., Beeline worker ID, Fieldglass contingent worker number). Used to map the internal worker record to the VMS worker profile during sync and reconciliation. Distinct from the internal worker_id.
reference: Beeline VMS Worker Profile; SAP Fieldglass Contingent Worker Module; SIA VMS Data Standards

description: The end date of the work week covered by the timesheet being synchronized. Together with work_week_start_date, defines the exact pay period for payroll and billing reconciliation.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act) Work Week Definition; Kronos Workforce Ready Pay Period Configuration; DOL Wage and Hour Division

description: The start date of the work week covered by the timesheet being synchronized. Used to align the sync record with the correct pay period and billing cycle for payroll processing and client invoicing.
reference: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act) Work Week Definition; Kronos Workforce Ready Pay Period Configuration; DOL Wage and Hour Division

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each individual punch event record in the Kronos Workforce Ready system. Serves as the immutable primary key for this append-only audit-grade event log. Role: EVENT_LOG.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 516 — Recordkeeping Requirements

description: Self-referencing identifier pointing to the original punch event record that this amended record corrects. Null for original (non-amended) punch events. Enables full amendment chain traceability for DOL audit defense and FLSA wage-and-hour dispute resolution. Supports the immutable append-only audit log pattern.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 516 — Recordkeeping; SOC 2 Type II — Audit Trail Requirements

description: Reference to the active placement or assignment under which the worker is clocking time. Associates the punch event to a specific client engagement, job order, and pay/bill rate context for downstream payroll and billing processing.
reference: ASA Staffing Standards; FLSA 29 CFR Part 516

description: Reference to the client cost center or department to which the worker's labor hours are allocated for this punch event. Supports labor cost distribution, client billing by department, and workforce analytics. Particularly relevant for transfer punch types where the worker moves between cost centers mid-shift.
reference: Oracle NetSuite ERP General Ledger; ASA Staffing Standards

description: Reference to the payroll pay period within which this punch event falls. Links the raw punch event to the TempWorks Payroll processing cycle for wage calculation, tax withholding, and W-2 reporting.
reference: IRS Publication 15 — Employer's Tax Guide; TempWorks Payroll Processing Module

description: Reference to the Kronos system user (supervisor, payroll admin, or system process) who created the amendment to this punch event. Null for original punch events. Supports accountability tracking and SOC 2 access control audit requirements.
reference: SOC 2 Type II — Change Management; FLSA 29 CFR Part 516

description: Reference to the contingent worker who performed the punch action. Links to the worker master record for identity resolution, payroll processing, and FLSA compliance reporting.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 516; ASA Workforce Standards

description: Reference to the Kronos scheduled shift that this punch event is associated with. Used to calculate schedule adherence, early/late arrival deviations, and unscheduled overtime. Null if the punch was not associated with a pre-defined schedule.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready Scheduling Module; ASA Workforce Management Standards

description: Foreign key linking to timesheet.time_entry. Business justification: punch_event captures raw clock-in/clock-out events from Kronos, while time_entry is the processed daily time record. Multiple punch events (clock in, clock out, break punches) contribute to a single t
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the parent timesheet record that aggregates this punch event into a daily or weekly time entry. Multiple punch events roll up into a single timesheet for approval and payroll processing.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 516; Kronos Workforce Ready Time and Attendance Module

description: Reference to the physical client worksite or facility where the worker is assigned and where the punch event occurred. Used for geofence configuration lookup, workers' compensation jurisdiction determination, and site-level labor analytics.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR Part 1904 — Recordkeeping; Workers Compensation State Regulations

description: Categorized reason code explaining why this punch event record was created as an amendment to a prior punch. Null for original punch events. Required for DOL audit defense and internal compliance review. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: missed_punch|device_failure|system_error|supervisor_correction|worker_request|schedule_adjustment|other — promote to reference product]
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 516; DOL Wage and Hour Division Audit Standards

description: The UTC timestamp when the amendment to this punch event was recorded in Kronos. Null for original punch events. Provides the audit trail timestamp for change management and DOL recordkeeping compliance.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 516; SOC 2 Type II — Audit Trail

description: The UTC timestamp when the punch event was approved by a supervisor or auto-approved by the system. Null if not yet approved. Marks the point at which the punch event becomes eligible for inclusion in payroll processing and client billing.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 516; Kronos Workforce Ready Approval Workflow

description: Indicates whether the hours associated with this punch event are billable to the client. True: hours are billable and will feed Salesforce Revenue Cloud invoicing; False: non-billable (e.g., orientation, training, administrative time). Drives client billing eligibility in the downstream billing pipeline.
reference: ASA Staffing Standards; Salesforce Revenue Cloud Billing Module

description: Indicates whether the punch event was authenticated via biometric verification (fingerprint scan, facial recognition) on the Kronos time clock. True: biometric match confirmed worker identity; False: biometric check failed or was bypassed. Null if the device does not support biometric authentication. Critical for buddy-punch prevention and FLSA compliance.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 516; CCPA Biometric Data Provisions; BIPA (Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act)

description: Unique identifier of the Kronos time clock hardware, mobile application instance, or web portal session that captured the punch event. Used for device-level audit trails, buddy-punch fraud detection, and equipment management. Sourced directly from the Kronos Workforce Ready device registry.
reference: SOC 2 Type II — Logical Access Controls; Kronos Workforce Ready Device Management

description: Indicates whether this punch event triggered one or more Kronos exception conditions (e.g., missed punch, early in, late out, geofence violation, unscheduled punch). True: one or more exceptions exist; False: no exceptions. Drives exception queue routing for supervisor review and payroll hold workflows.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready Exception Management; FLSA 29 CFR Part 516

description: The specific type of exception condition triggered by this punch event in Kronos. Examples include: missed_punch, early_in, late_in, early_out, late_out, long_break, short_break, geofence_violation, unscheduled_punch. Null if exception_flag is False. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: missed_punch|early_in|late_in|early_out|late_out|long_break|short_break|geofence_violation|unscheduled_punch — promote to reference product]
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready Exception Type Taxonomy; FLSA 29 CFR Part 516

business_glossary_term: FLSA (Fair Labor Standards Act) Workweek Start Date
description: The start date of the FLSA-defined 7-consecutive-day workweek period within which this punch event falls. The FLSA workweek is fixed and recurring, defined per employer or client site. Critical for accurate overtime calculation — OT is calculated per workweek, not per pay period.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 778.105 — Workweek Defined; DOL Wage and Hour Division

description: Indicates whether the punch event location coordinates fell within the approved geofence boundary for the assigned worksite at the time of the punch. True: worker was within the geofenced zone; False: worker was outside the boundary, triggering an exception alert. Null if geofence validation was not applicable (e.g., physical time clock punch).
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready Geofence Configuration; FLSA 29 CFR Part 516

description: Indicates whether a Kronos grace period rule was applied to this punch event, allowing a small window (e.g., 5 minutes) before or after the scheduled time without triggering an exception or early/late flag. Supports schedule adherence reporting accuracy.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready Grace Period Configuration; FLSA 29 CFR Part 785

description: The UTC timestamp when this punch event record was first ingested into the Databricks Silver layer from the Kronos source system. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED marker for data lineage, SLA monitoring of data pipeline latency, and audit trail completeness.
reference: SOC 2 Type II — Data Integrity; FLSA 29 CFR Part 516

description: The IP address of the device or network from which the punch event was submitted (applicable for web portal and mobile app punches). Used for fraud detection, buddy-punch investigation, and network-level audit trails. May be considered PII under GDPR and CCPA in some jurisdictions.
reference: GDPR Article 4; CCPA Section 1798.140; SOC 2 Type II — Logical Access Controls

description: The Kronos job code or labor category code associated with the work being performed at the time of the punch. Drives pay rate selection, bill rate application, and FLSA overtime classification. May change on a transfer punch when the worker switches tasks or roles mid-shift.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 541 — Exemptions; Kronos Workforce Ready Labor Distribution

description: The native punch event identifier assigned by the Kronos Workforce Ready source system. Preserved for cross-system reconciliation, data lineage tracing, and support ticket resolution. Enables exact record matching between the Databricks Silver layer and the Kronos operational system.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready API Documentation; SOC 2 Type II — Data Integrity

description: The UTC timestamp when this punch event record was last modified in the Databricks Silver layer (e.g., status update from raw to validated, amendment applied). Supports incremental data pipeline processing and audit trail completeness.
reference: SOC 2 Type II — Change Management; FLSA 29 CFR Part 516

description: GPS latitude coordinate (WGS-84 decimal degrees) captured at the moment of the punch event from a mobile device or GPS-enabled time clock. Used for geofence validation to confirm the worker was physically present at the designated worksite. Null if the device does not support GPS.
reference: WGS-84 Geodetic Standard; FLSA 29 CFR Part 516

description: The GPS accuracy radius in meters reported by the mobile device at the time of the punch event. Lower values indicate higher precision. Used to qualify geofence validation results — punches with accuracy radius exceeding the geofence boundary tolerance may be flagged for manual review.
reference: Kronos Workforce Ready Mobile GPS Specifications; WGS-84 Geodetic Standard

description: GPS longitude coordinate (WGS-84 decimal degrees) captured at the moment of the punch event from a mobile device or GPS-enabled time clock. Paired with latitude for geofence boundary validation and worksite presence verification.
reference: WGS-84 Geodetic Standard; FLSA 29 CFR Part 516

description: Classification of the pay category applicable to the hours captured by this punch event. regular: standard straight-time hours; overtime (OT): hours exceeding FLSA or state OT thresholds; double_time (DT): hours qualifying for double-time premium; per_diem: expense reimbursement-based pay; holiday: holiday premium pay; pto: Paid Time Off. Drives pay rate multiplier selection in TempWorks Payroll.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 778 — Overtime; TempWorks Payroll Pay Type Configuration; State Wage and Hour Laws

description: The channel or interface through which the punch event was submitted. time_clock: physical Kronos hardware terminal; mobile_app: Kronos mobile application; web_portal: browser-based Kronos portal; supervisor_entry: manually entered by a supervisor on behalf of the worker; api: submitted via system integration. Supports fraud detection and channel-level analytics.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 516; Kronos Workforce Ready Integration Specifications

description: Current processing state of the punch event record. raw: received from source device, not yet validated; validated: passed geofence, biometric, and schedule checks; amended: manually corrected by supervisor or payroll admin; rejected: failed validation rules; voided: nullified for audit purposes. Drives downstream time_entry aggregation eligibility.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 516; SOC 2 Type II — Change Management Controls

description: The exact UTC timestamp when the worker performed the clock action (punch-in, punch-out, break start, break end, or transfer). This is the authoritative real-world event time used for FLSA wage-and-hour calculations, DOL audit defense, and overtime determination. Stored in UTC per ISO 8601.
reference: FLSA 29 CFR Part 516; ISO 8601; DOL Wage and Hour Division

description: Discriminator indicating the nature of the clock action recorded. clock_in: worker begins a work period; clock_out: worker ends a work period; break_start: worker begins an unpaid or paid break; break_end: worker resumes work after a break; transfer: worker moves between cost centers, departments, or job codes mid-shift. Drives FLSA break compliance and hours calculation logic.
